items.title: Cognitive-behavioral therapy in people with Parkinson's disease and caregivers: A mixed method systematic review on clinical applications and therapeutic outcomes

ai.headline: CBT may help depression in people with Parkinson’s disease, but evidence for other symptoms is weak.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 54 studies looked at cognitive behavioural therapy for people with Parkinson’s disease and their caregivers. Moderate-certainty evidence supports CBT for depression, while evidence for anxiety, sleep, impulse control, cognition, motor symptoms and caregiver outcomes is limited or very uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which non-motor symptoms of Parkinson’s have stronger psychological support and where more research is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a qualified healthcare professional about whether CBT could be suitable for managing low mood related to Parkinson’s disease.
ai.fact: Moderate-certainty evidence from several randomised trials supports CBT for depression in people with Parkinson’s disease.

quiz.question: For which symptom does the review report moderate-certainty evidence that CBT is effective?
quiz.answer: Depression.

ai.caveat: The review includes studies of varying design and quality, and evidence for most outcomes beyond depression is low or very low certainty.

items.title: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Dietary and Physical Activity Behaviours Among Adolescents: A Systematic Review
items.venue: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics

ai.headline: Teenagers from wealthier backgrounds tend to eat healthier diets and join more organised physical activities.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 38 studies on how socioeconomic position relates to adolescents' eating and activity habits. It found that higher socioeconomic position was linked to healthier diets, more fruit and vegetables, and more organised physical activity, while lower socioeconomic position was linked to poorer diet quality, skipping breakfast, and eating more ultra-processed foods.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a young person's eating and activity habits are shaped by their family's social and economic circumstances, not just personal choice.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your local food options and activity opportunities might differ from those in other neighbourhoods.
ai.fact: Parental education was the socioeconomic indicator most consistently linked to adolescents' dietary behaviours.

quiz.question: Which behaviour showed inconsistent links to socioeconomic position according to the review?
quiz.answer: Associations with total physical activity and sedentary behaviour were inconsistent.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were observational, so they show links rather than prove that socioeconomic position causes these behaviours.

items.title: Effectiveness of home-based exercise interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.venue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

ai.headline: Home-based exercise improves heart and lung fitness in cancer survivors treated with cardiotoxic therapies.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at ten randomised trials involving 851 cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic treatments. Home-based exercise programmes significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak), but did not significantly improve six-minute walk distance or quality of life, and evidence on direct heart damage markers was limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that exercising at home may help cancer survivors maintain fitness after heart-harming treatments, though it cannot yet be said to prevent heart damage.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular home-based movement into your routine if you are recovering from cancer treatment, after checking with your care team.
ai.fact: Home-based exercise significantly improved VO2 peak by 2.35 mL/kg/min in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies.

quiz.question: What did home-based exercise significantly improve in cancer survivors according to the review?
quiz.answer: It significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness, measured as VO2 peak.

ai.caveat: The review is based on ten trials and direct heart damage outcomes were assessed in only one study, so firm conclusions about preventing heart toxicity cannot be drawn.

items.title: Family factors and school refusal among children and adolescents: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis

ai.headline: Family difficulties are modestly linked to school refusal in children and teenagers.
ai.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis combined results from studies on family factors and school refusal among children and adolescents. It found that greater family risk or lower family protection was positively associated with school refusal, though the strength of this link varied widely across studies.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that family context can matter when understanding why a young person avoids school, without proving that family problems cause the refusal.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether family stress or support patterns line up with school avoidance, and consider speaking with a trusted adult or professional if it persists.
ai.fact: Family risk and protection factors are associated with school refusal, but the evidence does not establish cause and effect.

quiz.question: What did the review find about family factors and school refusal?
quiz.answer: Greater family risk or lower family protection was positively associated with school refusal.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mostly observational, so it cannot show whether family difficulties cause school refusal or result from it.

items.title: How Much Active Learning? A Rapid Systematic Review of Contextual Moderators and an Evidence-Weighted Dosage Model for Political Science Teaching

ai.headline: Active learning boosts grades, but more isn't always better once you pass a moderate level.
ai.summary: A rapid review of 58 studies looked at how much active learning university courses should use. It found that mid- and high-intensity active learning bring similar grade gains, both well above low intensity, while closing achievement gaps seems to need high intensity. Effects are larger in small classes.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps students and teachers understand how to balance active learning with other teaching without assuming more is always better.
ai.life_skill: Try mixing active tasks like discussion or problem-solving into about half your study time rather than only listening or reading.
ai.fact: Meta-analyses link active learning in higher education to achievement gains of about half a standard deviation.

quiz.question: What did the review find about mid- versus high-intensity active learning?
quiz.answer: They produce similar achievement gains, both far above low intensity.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and a rapid review, so the evidence is not definitive.

items.title: Variation in recommendations for management of pediatric fever and neutropenia across databases and languages: A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines

ai.headline: Guidelines for children's fever with low white blood cells vary by language and database searched.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 14 clinical practice guidelines on managing fever with neutropenia in children. They found each database contained one unique guideline, only 36% were indexed in all three databases, and agreement with a reference guideline ranged from 33% to 100%.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that where and in what language clinicians look for guidance can change the advice they find, affecting care worldwide.
ai.life_skill: Check several trusted sources and languages when looking up health guidance rather than relying on one database.
ai.fact: Fever with neutropenia is a common complication of cancer therapy in children linked to serious illness, death, and high resource use.

quiz.question: What percentage of the 14 guidelines were indexed in all three databases?
quiz.answer: Only 36% (5 out of 14) were indexed in all three databases.

ai.caveat: The review included only 14 guidelines from the last 10 years and did not prove that database or language restrictions directly cause worse patient outcomes.

items.title: Dyslexia extends beyond reading difficulties: genetic links with social functioning and well-being

ai.headline: Genetic liability to dyslexia is linked to lower life satisfaction, loneliness, and less workplace support.
ai.summary: Researchers combined genetic and survey data from the Lifelines cohort with public genome-wide study results to examine links between dyslexia and social traits. They found that dyslexia was associated with lower life satisfaction, higher loneliness, and less collegial support at work, and that genetic liability to dyslexia predicted increased loneliness and social isolation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that dyslexia may affect social and emotional wellbeing beyond reading and spelling, suggesting a need for broader support throughout life.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether reading difficulties are affecting your social confidence or sense of connection, and consider speaking with a trusted adult or professional about support.
ai.fact: Dyslexia is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterised by persistent difficulties in reading and spelling.

quiz.question: What did the study find about the direction of the relationship between dyslexia and social outcomes?
quiz.answer: The evidence pointed from dyslexia toward adverse social and wellbeing outcomes, not the other way around.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it is observational, so it cannot prove causation on its own.

items.title: Convergent genome- and gene-level constraints shape repeated environmental adaptation in grasses

ai.headline: Grasses adapt to extreme environments through predictable genetic changes across many species.
ai.summary: The study examined 687 grass genomes from 561 species across 17 climate zones. It found that grasses repeatedly shift similar genome-wide properties and use the same genes when adapting to extreme temperature, water, and soil conditions.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how plants survive harsh conditions, which matters for food security and ecosystems.
ai.fact: Grasses show repeated, predictable genetic changes when adapting to extreme environments.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about how grasses adapt to extreme environments?
quiz.answer: Grasses repeatedly use similar genetic changes across many species when adapting to extreme temperature, water, and soil conditions.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Factors Associated with Meaning in Life Among Hispanic Adults in the Post-Pandemic Period: A Cross-Sectional Study Across 16 Countries

ai.headline: About half of Hispanic adults across 16 countries reported low meaning in life after the pandemic.
ai.summary: A cross-sectional study of 10,142 Hispanic adults aged 18 to 78 across 16 countries examined meaning in life after the pandemic. It found that 50.2% had low meaning in life, while mental health, occupational purpose, gratitude, friendships, and meaningful activities were linked to higher meaning, and low perceived workplace success, lack of gratitude, and heavy social media use were linked to lower meaning.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling a sense of meaning may depend more on everyday habits and relationships than on income or education.
ai.life_skill: Notice which activities and friendships make your life feel meaningful and make time for them regularly.
ai.fact: In this study, income, education, and gender were not significantly associated with meaning in life.

quiz.question: What percentage of participants experienced low levels of meaning in life?
quiz.answer: 50.2% of participants experienced low levels of meaning in life.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and because it is cross-sectional it cannot show that the linked factors actually cause changes in meaning in life.

items.title: AI may help tailor treatment for childhood brain tumors

ai.headline: An AI model may help doctors choose more precise treatments for children with malignant brain tumors.
ai.summary: Researchers developed an artificial intelligence model to help balance effective cancer treatment with avoiding lasting side effects on learning, development and quality of life. The model may support doctors in making treatment decisions with greater precision.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could one day improve care for children with serious illnesses by weighing treatment benefits against long-term harms.

quiz.question: What did the researchers develop to help with childhood brain tumor treatment decisions?
quiz.answer: They developed an artificial intelligence model that may help doctors make those decisions with greater precision.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a model that may help; it is not peer-reviewed evidence that the model works in practice.

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence

ai.headline: Researchers propose AI companions that stay with a person lifelong to extend human thinking and memory.
ai.summary: This is a theory paper, not a study with data. It argues that AI should move beyond autonomous agents to become embedded, lifelong “cognitive symbionts” that sense a person’s context, remember their history, and think alongside them to close the gap between what people could know and what working memory can hold.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a new way to think about how AI might support everyday memory, decisions and learning rather than just replacing human tasks.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you forget something useful and consider whether a trusted digital tool could help you capture it for later.
ai.fact: The paper introduces “AI-augmented human intelligence” as the idea of measuring how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person.

quiz.question: What does the paper call an AI system that stays with a person lifelong and thinks alongside them?
quiz.answer: It calls it a cognitive symbiont.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint theory paper with no data or experiments, so the ideas are untested proposals rather than proven findings.

items.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval

ai.headline: A new AI method improves image search by imagining how to change a picture before matching it.
ai.summary: The paper studies composed image retrieval, where a user finds a target image using a reference image plus a text description of changes. It introduces FactEmbed, which separates understanding the requested visual change from creating a search-friendly image representation, and reports better results than earlier methods on retrieval benchmarks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI image search can be made more accurate by breaking a request into imagined visual steps before matching images.
ai.life_skill: Try describing the exact change you want when searching for an image, rather than only naming the subject.
ai.fact: FactEmbed uses factorized latents to simulate intended visual modifications before forming discriminative embeddings for retrieval.

quiz.question: What does FactEmbed do before forming a search-friendly image representation?
quiz.answer: It uses factorized latents to simulate the intended visual modifications and ground into target semantics.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so its claims are not yet independently confirmed.

items.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries

ai.headline: Preprimary education eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes and greater reproductive autonomy for women across 117 low- and middle-income countries.
ai.summary: The study looked at eligibility for preprimary education in 117 low- and middle-income countries. It found that eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how early childhood education policies may be connected to women’s opportunities and life choices around the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how access to early education can shape opportunities for girls and women in your community.
ai.fact: Preprimary education eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes and greater reproductive autonomy for women across 117 low- and middle-income countries.

quiz.question: What did the study find is linked to eligibility for preprimary education across 117 low- and middle-income countries?
quiz.answer: Eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing.

ai.caveat: The findings show a link, not proof that preprimary education causes these changes, because the study is observational.

items.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial

ai.headline: A small trial tested ivonescimab alone or with chemotherapy before lung cancer surgery and found promising responses in both groups.
ai.summary: In a nonrandomised phase 2 trial, patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer received ivonescimab either alone or with chemotherapy around the time of surgery. Both groups showed encouraging pathological response rates, and sustained circulating tumour DNA negativity during neoadjuvant therapy may predict response.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how new cancer treatments are tested and how blood DNA might one day help track treatment response.
ai.fact: Sustained circulating tumour DNA negativity throughout neoadjuvant therapy may be predictive of response in resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
ai.caveat: The study was nonrandomised and phase 2, so it cannot prove that ivonescimab causes better outcomes or that ctDNA negativity predicts response.

items.title: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response

ai.headline: Children who eat more ultra-processed foods show stronger brain reward responses to tempting foods and gain more body fat over a year.
ai.summary: USC researchers studied 46 children aged 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods had greater activity in the brain's reward system when looking at foods like cookies and French fries. These stronger brain responses were linked to larger increases in body fat and BMI one year later.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that ultra-processed diets may affect how children's brains respond to food cues, which could help explain the link between these diets and weight gain.
ai.life_skill: Notice how often you choose ultra-processed snacks and try swapping some for less processed options.
ai.fact: In this study, children who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger brain reward responses to tempting foods and greater increases in body fat and BMI one year later.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about children who ate more ultra-processed foods?
quiz.answer: They showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods and had greater increases in body fat and BMI one year later.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study with a small group of children, so it shows a link but cannot prove that ultra-processed foods caused the brain changes or weight gain.

items.title: Delivering a Digital Health Intervention to Improve Food Access and Dietary Quality Among Adults With Hypertension

ai.headline: A trial will test whether grocery delivery plus coaching helps people with high blood pressure eat better.
ai.summary: The study plans to enrol 65 adults with hypertension and limited access to quality food. It will test a four-month programme combining grocery delivery membership, weekly list recommendations, skills training, goal setting, food tracking, text feedback and health coaching against the DASH eating pattern.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how practical support with food shopping and eating habits might help people manage high blood pressure in daily life.
ai.life_skill: Try planning a weekly grocery list and tracking what you eat to see how it matches healthy eating guidance.
ai.fact: The DASH eating pattern is a dietary approach designed to help stop hypertension.

quiz.question: What is the main goal of the study?
quiz.answer: To test whether the programme is feasible and acceptable, and whether it improves DASH adherence and blood pressure.

ai.caveat: This is a trial registration with planned results, not a completed study with reported findings.

items.title: Scientists discover surprising heart benefits of eating avocado and mango every day

ai.headline: Eating avocado and mango daily may improve heart health in adults with prediabetes.
ai.summary: A study involving adults with prediabetes found that consuming an avocado and a cup of mango every day for eight weeks improved blood vessel function and diastolic blood pressure. These benefits were observed without weight gain or changes in calorie intake.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that simple dietary swaps can support cardiovascular health without requiring strict calorie counting or weight loss.
ai.life_skill: Consider adding nutrient-rich fruits like avocado and mango to your daily diet to support heart health.
ai.fact: The study found that the combination of avocado and mango improved blood vessel function and diastolic blood pressure in participants.

quiz.question: Did the participants in the study gain weight while eating avocado and mango daily?
quiz.answer: No, the benefits occurred without weight gain or changes in calorie intake.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a single study, so the findings are not yet confirmed by independent replication or peer-reviewed systematic reviews.

items.title: Naseem Salahuddin: infectious disease specialist who fought rabies in Pakistan

ai.headline: A Pakistani doctor used a combined human and animal health approach to fight rabies.
ai.summary: This profile describes how infectious disease specialist Naseem Salahuddin tackled rabies in Pakistan, where about 1,000 people die annually. She implemented the 'One Health' approach, combining mass dog vaccination, public awareness, and improved surveillance to reduce deaths.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that solving complex health problems often requires looking at the connection between people, animals, and the environment, not just treating individual patients.
ai.life_skill: Notice how health issues in your community might be linked to animal or environmental factors.
ai.fact: Rabies in Pakistan is largely a disease of children, with an estimated 1,000 deaths per year.

quiz.question: What specific strategy did Naseem Salahuddin use to address rabies?
quiz.answer: She introduced the One Health approach, which integrates human, animal, and environmental health strategies.

ai.caveat: This is a biographical profile and obituary, not a research study, so it does not provide statistical proof of the initiative's effectiveness.

items.title: The Effects of Monetary Policy on Macroeconomic Expectations: High-Frequency Evidence from Prediction Markets -- by Eric T. Swanson, Wang Renxuan, Yanbin Wu

ai.headline: Interest rate rises lead prediction markets to expect lower output, jobs and inflation, with little Fed information effect.
ai.summary: Researchers used prices from a US prediction market to see how Federal Reserve interest rate announcements change expectations about the economy. They found that rate rises led markets to expect lower output, employment and inflation, matching standard economic theory. There was little evidence of a separate 'Fed Information Effect'.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how interest rate decisions shape economic expectations helps people make sense of news about jobs, prices and the cost of borrowing.
ai.life_skill: Notice how central bank interest rate announcements shift expectations about jobs and prices.
ai.fact: Prediction market prices can reveal how quickly expectations about output, employment and inflation respond to interest rate announcements.

quiz.question: What did prediction markets expect to happen to output, employment and inflation when the Federal Reserve raised interest rates?
quiz.answer: They expected output, employment and inflation to fall, consistent with standard monetary policy transmission.

ai.caveat: This is a single preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the results should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: North Atlantic's 'cold blob' may contain climate nuance

ai.headline: A North Atlantic 'cold blob' cooled while other oceans warmed over the past century.
ai.summary: Researchers examined a large area south and southeast of Greenland known as the cold blob. It cooled by as much as 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit over the past century even as other ocean waters warmed. Observers have long linked this area's temperature to the strength of a major ocean current.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that parts of the ocean can cool even as the planet warms overall, which matters for understanding global climate patterns.
ai.fact: A North Atlantic area south and southeast of Greenland cooled by as much as 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit over the past century while other ocean waters warmed.

quiz.question: What happened to the North Atlantic cold blob over the past century?
quiz.answer: It cooled by as much as 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit while other ocean waters warmed.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed study, so it does not prove cause or predict future changes.

items.title: Estimating bone marrow adiposity from head MRI and identifying its genetic architecture

ai.headline: Existing head MRI scans can reveal skull bone marrow fat and its genetic links.
ai.summary: Researchers trained an artificial neural network to spot bone marrow fat in the skull using existing head MRI scans. Across large datasets, the trait was highly heritable, linked to 41 genetic regions, and also linked to cognitive ability and Parkinson's disease.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that brain scans already collected for research could reveal hidden clues about bone health and brain conditions.
ai.fact: Bone marrow fat inside the skull changes through life and differs between males and females, including around menopause.

quiz.question: What did the researchers measure in head MRI scans besides the brain?
quiz.answer: They measured bone marrow fat in the skull using an artificial neural network.

ai.caveat: Because the study is observational, it can show links but cannot prove that bone marrow fat causes cognitive ability or Parkinson's disease.

items.title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force

ai.headline: Delhi's air quality index reached 377, classed as "very poor," ahead of Diwali.

ai.fact: An air quality index reading of 377 is classified as "very poor".

quiz.answer: It stood at 377, in the "very poor" category.

items.title: This cholesterol drug promised to be a game-changer. Why did it flop in the clinic — and is there still hope?

ai.headline: A drug that lowers lipoprotein(a) failed to show benefit in a major trial.
ai.summary: Doctors hoped drugs cutting lipoprotein(a), a substance linked to heart disease, would prevent heart problems. A major trial of one such therapy did not show a benefit. Researchers are now trying to understand why lowering the risk factor did not help.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that lowering a blood marker linked to disease does not always improve health, so treatments must be tested in people before being widely used.
ai.fact: Lipoprotein(a) is an important cardiovascular risk factor.

quiz.question: What happened in the major trial of a therapy that lowers lipoprotein(a)?
quiz.answer: It failed to show a benefit.

items.title: For early-career scientists, the cost of AI can be a problem

ai.headline: AI tools can be cheap or free for some researchers but costly or out of reach for others
ai.summary: The article looks at early-career scientists and their access to AI tools. It reports that some researchers get top tools for next to nothing, while others pay out of pocket or go without.

quiz.answer: Some researchers get top tools for next to nothing, while others pay out of pocket or go without.

items.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop a wearable monitor for early disease detection

ai.headline: Wearable monitor for disease detection
ai.summary: A team led by MIT has received funding to develop a wearable monitor for early disease detection. The monitor aims to measure heart failure and sepsis biomarkers in real-time. The team has been awarded up to $38 million for this project.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because early disease detection can improve health outcomes and save lives.
ai.fact: A wearable monitor can potentially measure heart failure and sepsis biomarkers in real-time.

quiz.answer: To measure heart failure and sepsis biomarkers in real-time.

ai.headline: Text-based AI helped idea generation, while image-based AI helped knowledge, but no sequence won overall.

ai.why_it_matters: It shows that different AI tools may suit different stages of a creative task, but no single sequence guarantees a better final result.
ai.life_skill: Try using text-based AI when brainstorming ideas and image-based AI when refining visual details, then judge the result yourself.

ai.caveat: The study bundled AI modality with interaction and interface features, and the knowledge assessments had limited reliability, so isolated modality effects or durable learning are not established.

items.title: Implementation of WHO Self-Help Plus among Ukrainian university students during wartime: A multicenter longitudinal study

items.title: Childhood educational, social and health factors associated with the timing and recurrence of NEET status into adulthood: a prospective birth cohort study

ai.headline: Childhood education, trauma, conduct problems and depression are linked to later NEET patterns.
ai.summary: This study followed over 8,000 young people from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children, looking at childhood educational, social and health factors and later NEET status between ages 16 and 33. Higher attainment at age 10-11 was linked to fewer NEET episodes, while childhood traumas, persistent conduct problems and adolescent depression were linked to more accumulated, sustained or recurrent NEET.

items.title: Validating static food web model diet matrices using stable isotope simulation

ai.headline: A new computer method checks whether food web diet models match long-term eating patterns shown by stable isotopes.
ai.summary: The study tested a way to validate diet matrices used in ecosystem models like Ecopath with Ecosim by simulating stable isotope signatures and comparing them with real carbon and sulphur measurements. It found agreement in isotope space but mismatches in energy pathways, with differences in species coverage between stomach contents and isotope data driving some of the disagreement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how scientists can improve models used to manage fisheries and ecosystems, which affects food supplies and environmental decisions.
ai.life_skill: Check where your information comes from before trusting a conclusion.
ai.fact: Stable isotopes give a time-integrated view of average diets, unlike stomach contents which show only recent meals.

quiz.question: What did the researchers compare to validate diet models?
quiz.answer: They compared simulated stable isotope signatures with empirical delta-13C and delta-34S measurements.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and is based on a single case-study model from the Northern Gulf of Mexico.

items.title: High net coverage, incomplete protection: factors associated with malaria resurgence in three elimination districts of Zimbabwe1. Rameck Makokove, Plan International Zimbabwe, Malaria Prevention Control and Elimination Programme

ai.headline: Malaria returned in three Zimbabwe districts despite high net ownership because nets were not used consistently and mosquitoes bite outdoors.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 314 household heads and sampled mosquitoes in Masvingo, Chegutu and Gokwe South. Most people knew malaria spreads through mosquitoes and owned nets, but only 49% slept under one the previous night, use was seasonal, and many could not get replacements; mosquitoes were active indoors and outdoors during peak biting times.
ai.why_it_matters: Owning a protective tool does not guarantee protection if it is not used regularly or if exposure happens outside net coverage.
ai.life_skill: Check whether your protective habits match the times and places you are actually exposed to risk.
ai.fact: Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles funestus mosquitoes were found biting both indoors and outdoors in the study districts.

quiz.question: What percentage of people who owned nets reported sleeping under one the previous night?
quiz.answer: Only 49% reported sleeping under a net the previous night.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and a single cross-sectional survey, so it shows links rather than proof of cause and effect.

items.title: Pediatric emergency medicine in Lebanon: Physician-perceived comfort levels, challenges, and educational needs

ai.headline: Doctors in Lebanon report gaps in training and resources for children's emergency care.
ai.summary: A survey of 59 Lebanese physicians who treat children in emergencies found most felt comfortable with fluid management and X-rays, but fewer felt confident with procedures such as suturing, fracture care and ultrasound. Nearly all supported creating a dedicated paediatric emergency medicine fellowship.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how training and equipment gaps can affect the safety of emergency care for children in one country.

items.title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence

ai.headline: AI models can solve tasks alone but often struggle to work well as teammates.
ai.summary: Researchers tested 18 AI models on 240 teamwork tasks drawn from aviation, medicine, coding and negotiations. Every model showed weaknesses as a teammate, with the best scoring only 82.2 out of 100, and general capability did not guarantee good teamwork.
ai.why_it_matters: As AI agents increasingly work alongside people and other agents, their ability to collaborate safely and reliably matters for everyday tasks and decisions.

ai.fact: The best AI model scored 82.2 out of 100 on a benchmark measuring teamwork.

items.title: Sadomasochistic surgeon barred from seeing female patients wins High Court ruling

ai.headline: A surgeon won a High Court ruling lifting practice restrictions linked to his private consensual sexual activity.
ai.summary: A consultant transplant surgeon challenged interim conditions imposed by a tribunal while the General Medical Council investigated his fitness to practise. The conditions had barred him from face-to-face consultations with female patients except in life-threatening emergencies. ai.life_skill: Check whether a workplace rule is based on actual evidence of risk before accepting it as fair.
ai.fact: Interim orders tribunals can place conditions on doctors while a fitness-to-practise investigation is pending.

quiz.question: What did the High Court ruling do to the conditions on the surgeon's practice?
quiz.answer: It lifted the interim conditions, including the bar on face-to-face consultations with female patients except in life-threatening emergencies.

items.title: Even moderate drinking linked to cancer and early death, major study finds

ai.headline: Even moderate drinking is linked to cancer, heart disease and early death, with no overall health benefits found.
ai.summary: A major study examined alcohol consumption and health outcomes. It found that even small amounts of alcohol increase the risk of cancer, heart disease and premature death, and that drinking more than one alcoholic beverage per day significantly raises long-term health risks.
ai.why_it_matters: This challenges the common belief that moderate drinking is harmless or beneficial, helping people make more informed choices about alcohol.

items.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half

ai.headline: An experimental drug rejuvenated aging liver cells in rats, cutting an Alzheimer’s-linked protein and lowering bad cholesterol.
ai.summary: USC researchers studied aging liver cells in rats treated with an experimental drug. The treatment restored the cells, halved levels of an Alzheimer’s-linked protein, reduced bad cholesterol to youthful levels, and revived a communication system that helps liver cells clear harmful substances from the bloodstream.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests liver health may be linked to brain and heart health, though this has only been shown in rats so far.
ai.fact: Aging liver cells in rats can be restored by an experimental drug, which also lowered an Alzheimer’s-linked protein and bad cholesterol.

quiz.question: What happened to the Alzheimer’s-linked protein after the experimental drug was given to rats?
quiz.answer: Its levels were cut in half.

items.title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection

ai.headline: Scientists found three gene regulators that can push immune cells from an M1 to an M2 state and make them more vulnerable to a common bacterium.
ai.summary: The study used computer analysis of macrophage responses to 28 different stimuli to identify regulatory factors controlling immune cell states. Knocking down three factors—CEBPB, NFE2L2 and BCL3—in human macrophage-like cells shifted them away from an M1 inflammatory state toward an M2 state, even when exposed to an M1 trigger. These cells then became more susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how immune cells decide their role in inflammation and infection, which helps scientists understand immune balance and disease.
ai.fact: Macrophages can be steered toward different functional states, such as M1 or M2, by specific gene regulators.

quiz.question: What happened when researchers knocked down the three regulatory factors in macrophage-like cells exposed to an M1 stimulant?
quiz.answer: The cells did not shift fully to an M1 state, instead showed more M2 markers, and became more susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection.

ai.caveat: This is a single laboratory study using human cell lines and computer modelling, so the findings are not yet proof of how immune cells behave in people.

items.title: Affirmative Action, Faculty Productivity and Caste Interactions: Evidence from Engineering Colleges in India -- by Robert W. Fairlie, Saurabh Khanna, Prashant Loyalka, Gagandeep S. Sachdeva

ai.headline: Faculty hired under India’s caste-based hiring quotas teach as well as other faculty despite having fewer qualifications.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 50 engineering colleges in India where about half of faculty hires are reserved for disadvantaged caste and social class groups. Reservation-category faculty had less education, lower rank and less experience, but their students achieved similar grades, attendance, dropout rates and graduation outcomes, with slightly better course grades in some cases. Research productivity and administrative service also showed no meaningful differences.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that hiring quotas for disadvantaged groups do not necessarily lower workplace performance, which matters for debates about affirmative action in many countries.
ai.life_skill: Notice that someone’s background or entry route does not automatically predict how well they do a job.
ai.fact: Indian engineering colleges are required to reserve about half of faculty hires for individuals from disadvantaged caste and social class groups.

quiz.question: Did students taught by reservation-category faculty perform worse than those taught by general-category faculty?
quiz.answer: No, they performed similarly or slightly better on course grades, with no meaningful differences across other outcomes.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings come from observational data in Indian engineering colleges, so they cannot prove that quotas cause equal performance.

items.title: AI measurements of heart scans more strongly linked to patient survival than clinician measurements

items.title: The effects of physical activity interventions on preschoolers' self-regulation skills: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

ai.headline: Physical activity programmes can improve self-regulation in preschool children, especially in groups.
ai.summary: Researchers combined 25 randomised trials of physical activity programmes for preschoolers aged 18 months to nearly six years. items.title: Digital health misinformation in Southeast Asia: a systematic review of susceptibility, public health consequences, and intervention evidence

ai.headline: A review of studies in Southeast Asia links digital health misinformation to beliefs, sharing, vaccine attitudes, preventive behavior, distress, and delayed care.
ai.summary: The review examined 77 reports from Southeast Asia on digital health misinformation. It found that judging and believing misinformation was linked to thinking skills, literacy, trust, identity, emotion, and social context, while misinformation-related constructs were linked to sharing, vaccine attitudes, preventive behavior, distress, and delayed care. Correction, inoculation, digital education, chatbots, and community responses had mixed results, with most not isolating a misinformation-specific behavioral effect.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that online health claims can shape real health choices and wellbeing, so checking sources matters before acting on health advice.

items.title: New money, no money, and psychological inheritance in the elasticity of 21st century happiness

ai.headline: Money is linked to happiness worldwide, but childhood economic class shapes how strongly that link holds in adulthood.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed data from 91 countries and over 53,000 people. They found a positive association between income and well-being that is strongest in wealthier countries and when incomes rise above local living costs, while childhood economic class continues to influence adult well-being even after upward mobility.

ai.summary: Researchers studied the link between food insecurity and psychological health in 6,695 US adults. They found that food insecurity is more common among lower socioeconomic groups and is associated with poorer psychological health. items.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation

ai.headline: A new AI system lets humans and software agents share and edit work files together over long tasks.
ai.summary: CoworkOS is a preprint study of a general-purpose harness for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management. It lets humans and AI agents inspect and revise the same documents, presentations, CAD models and Blender scenes through conversation or direct modification, with persistent memory so work can be paused and resumed. items.title: Negotiating epistemic authority in AI-assisted lesson planning: a multiple-case study of preservice mathematics teachers

ai.headline: AI lesson-planning help can lead trainee teachers to hand over decisions without realising it.
ai.summary: Researchers studied five trainee maths teachers in China as they planned lessons using generative AI. items.title: Effects of water quality, sanitation, handwashing and nutritional interventions on enteric pathogen seroconversion in rural Kenya: a cluster randomised trial

ai.headline: Household water, sanitation and nutrition programmes did not meaningfully reduce childhood gut infections in rural Kenya.
ai.summary: Researchers tested whether improving water, sanitation, handwashing and nutrition lowered infection markers in young children. Differences between groups were tiny, and none met the statistical threshold for a reliable effect after multiple comparisons.

items.title: Oleic acid suppresses NLRP3 inflammasome activation to prevent dermal macrophage death and limit imiquimod-induced psoriasis

ai.headline: Oleic acid may protect skin immune cells and reduce psoriasis-like inflammation in mice.
ai.summary: Researchers studied mice with psoriasis-like skin inflammation and tested oral oleic acid, a fatty acid. Oleic acid reduced skin thickening, preserved skin-resident macrophages, lowered inflammatory markers, and stopped macrophage death by dampening NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.

items.title: Burden of newly diagnosed hypertension and potential 10-year cardiovascular risk in Burundi: A Bayesian logistic regression and Framingham score-based study

items.title: Vitamins E and C supplementation reduces hepatic lipid peroxidation and steatosis in neonatal Yucatan piglets receiving prolonged parenteral nutrition

items.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
