ai.summary: A review of 33 studies involving over 211,000 people examined medicines for grief and bereavement-related depression. No medication reduced grief symptoms in controlled studies, and overall effects on depression were small and not statistically significant. The research quality was generally low.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows that pills are not a proven remedy for grief, so people should not expect medication alone to ease loss.
ai.life_skill: Speak with a GP or bereavement counsellor about non-medication support if grief feels overwhelming.
ai.fact: No current medication has been shown to reduce grief symptoms in controlled studies.

quiz.question: Did any medication reduce grief symptoms in the controlled studies reviewed?
quiz.answer: No, no medications reduced grief symptomatology across any controlled studies.

ai.caveat: The included studies were mostly low quality and reported data inconsistently, so the findings are not definitive.

items.title: The Critique of Pure Information

ai.headline: Political deception is about more than false information—it involves rhetoric, style, and how people receive it.
ai.summary: The book examines disinformation, misinformation, and post-truth politics. It argues that deception works through rhetoric, style, image-text composition, platform circulation, emotion, and public uptake—not just false content. It concludes that fact-checking, media literacy, platform governance, or AI detection alone cannot fix democratic communication.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that judging a message requires looking at how it is framed, shared, and felt, not only whether its claims are true.
ai.life_skill: Notice how a message is framed, shared, and emotionally presented before deciding whether to trust it.
ai.fact: Deceptive communication can rely on style, emotion, and presentation as much as on false statements.

quiz.question: What does the book say cannot repair democratic communication by itself?
quiz.answer: Fact-checking, media literacy, platform governance, or AI detection alone cannot do it.

ai.caveat: This is a single scholarly book’s theoretical argument, not experimental proof of cause and effect.

items.title: Bringing developmental science closer to families: Caregivers’ and professionals’ perspectives on participation in early childhood research

ai.headline: Online child research can include more families if researchers protect privacy and offer useful feedback.
ai.summary: Researchers held four focus groups with ten caregivers and twelve professionals to explore barriers to taking part in early childhood studies. Families worried about privacy and how children’s images would be used, while professionals noted that families facing many challenges can be wary of authority. Online participation was welcomed if researchers gave material help and support, and families valued developmental feedback and resources more than money.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how researchers can make child development studies more accessible and trustworthy for families who are often left out.
ai.life_skill: Before joining a research study, check how your privacy and your child’s images will be protected.
ai.fact: Families taking part in early childhood research often value developmental feedback and resources more than financial payments.

quiz.question: What did families value more than financial incentives in early childhood research?
quiz.answer: They valued developmental feedback and resources more than money.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and is based on a small number of focus groups, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Household Food Waste in Urban Bahawalpur, Pakistan: Women's Food Management Practices, Maqasid al-Shariah, and Resource Sustainability

ai.headline: In Pakistan, women who track spending waste less food, but shared shopping duties increase waste.
ai.summary: This study surveyed 424 households in urban Bahawalpur, Pakistan, to see what drives the disposal of chapatti (flatbread). It found that women who frequently monitored household food expenditure were associated with significantly lower odds of wasting food, whereas sharing food-purchasing responsibility was linked to higher waste.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that simple habits like tracking spending and clear roles in meal planning can reduce household waste, a key factor in food security and environmental sustainability.
ai.life_skill: Try keeping a simple record of what you buy for food to see where your money and resources are going.
ai.fact: In the studied Pakistani households, 59.7% reported wasting chapatti, with joint households showing lower waste rates than nuclear families.

quiz.question: According to the study, how did shared food-purchasing responsibility affect the likelihood of food waste?
quiz.answer: Shared food-purchasing responsibility was associated with a 61.3% increase in the odds of wastage compared to sole female responsibility.

ai.caveat: The data is self-reported and cross-sectional, so the study shows associations rather than proving that these factors directly cause the waste.

items.title: IAMRAGBENCH: Benchmarking Authorization Expansions in LLM-Generated AWS IAM Policies under RAG Poisoning

ai.headline: AI tools can be tricked into creating cloud security rules that accidentally grant extra access.
ai.summary: Researchers tested how easily AI systems could be manipulated into generating cloud security policies that allow more access than intended. They found that when specific misleading information was included, the AI frequently created rules that violated security boundaries, even though the rules looked technically valid.
ai.why_it_matters: As people increasingly use AI to manage digital infrastructure, understanding that these tools can be manipulated is crucial for maintaining security and trust in automated systems.
ai.life_skill: Treat AI-generated technical solutions as drafts that require independent verification by a qualified expert before use.
ai.fact: AI systems using retrieval-augmented generation can be induced to produce valid but overly permissive security policies when exposed to attacker-controlled context.

quiz.question: What did the study find happens when AI is exposed to specific misleading context?
quiz.answer: The AI produced security policies that technically worked but granted more access than was safely intended.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint benchmark study, not a peer-reviewed trial, and the results depend on specific test conditions that may not reflect all real-world scenarios.

items.title: Evaluation of a six-item second-order academic engagement model in Ecuadorian university students

ai.headline: A shorter six-item version of a student engagement scale worked well for Ecuadorian university students.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a shortened six-item version of the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale for Students with 1,732 Ecuadorian university students. The shorter scale showed strong reliability and fit the data well overall, though one fit measure was higher than ideal.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a brief questionnaire can reliably measure student engagement across different groups, which can help schools and researchers understand student wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice what makes you feel engaged or disengaged in your studies and reflect on those patterns.
ai.fact: Academic engagement is linked to students’ wellbeing and academic success.

quiz.question: How many university students took part in the study?
quiz.answer: The study included 1,732 university students from three Ecuadorian universities.

ai.caveat: This was a single cross-sectional study in Ecuador, so the results need independent replication before the shorter scale can be considered an established alternative.

items.title: Which Attention Helps? A Slide-Level Ablation of Attention-Augmented CNNs for Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Grading

ai.headline: AI can help grade ovarian cancer slides, but results are more modest than often claimed when data leakage is avoided.
ai.summary: Researchers tested several AI models on 259 whole-slide images of serous ovarian carcinoma to distinguish high-grade from low-grade tumours. A pretrained model performed best, while adding finer attention branches or using a pathology foundation model did not improve results.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how careful study design affects the reliability of AI tools used in cancer diagnosis.
ai.life_skill: Check whether health-related AI claims are based on studies that avoid mixing training and testing data.
ai.fact: A colour-only classifier reached AUC 0.66, suggesting some tumour separability comes from stain and colour rather than tissue structure.

quiz.question: Which model performed best in the study?
quiz.answer: The ImageNet-pretrained MobileNet with a differential-attention module performed best.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and with only 42 low-grade slides the study may be underpowered to detect finer differences.

items.title: Interpreting graph neural networks reveals microbial association patterns in inflammatory bowel diseases

ai.headline: Patterns of how gut microbes connect may signal inflammatory bowel disease better than microbe counts alone.
ai.summary: Researchers used graph neural networks on gut microbiome data from 106 people to study how microbes associate with each other in inflammatory bowel disease. The models found a tightly connected group of Bacteroidales species that predicted disease even though their individual abundance did not differ between people with and without IBD. Removing these associations made predictions nearly random in an independent group.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that looking at relationships between gut microbes, not just which microbes are present, can reveal hidden patterns in diseases like IBD.
ai.life_skill: Notice that health findings often come from patterns and connections, not just single isolated facts.
ai.fact: A densely connected module of co-abundant Bacteroidales species carried most of the predictive signal for IBD in an independent cohort.

quiz.question: Did the Bacteroidales species identified by the graph neural network differ in abundance between people with and without IBD?
quiz.answer: No, these species were not differentially abundant between conditions.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the findings come from observational data, so they cannot prove that the microbial patterns cause IBD.

items.title: Asymmetric Housing Co-adaptation Reshapes Neighborhood Recovery Trajectories after Hurricanes

ai.headline: Neighbourhood repair and sale decisions after hurricanes influence each other in different ways over time.
ai.summary: Researchers studied more than 1.3 million households across nearly 2,800 communities after Hurricanes Harvey, Ida and Ian. They found that neighbours’ repair choices tend to reinforce each other early on, while neighbours’ decisions to sell can make nearby repairs less likely, especially after Hurricane Ian.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how one household’s choice to sell or repair can ripple through a neighbourhood and shape how a whole area recovers after a disaster.
ai.life_skill: Notice how neighbours’ decisions after a storm might affect your own repair or sale plans.
ai.fact: After Hurricane Ian, a greater history of sales among connected neighbours was linked to a lower probability of repair in almost every community studied.

quiz.question: What did the study find about neighbours’ sale decisions and repair decisions after Hurricane Ian?
quiz.answer: A greater sale history among connected neighbours was linked to a lower probability of repair in almost every community.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Cohort Profile: The Adolescent and Young Adult Tracking Engagement and Management Skills (AYA TEAMS) longitudinal cohort of childhood cancer survivors in the United States

ai.headline: A US study is tracking young adult childhood cancer survivors to understand what helps them manage their own long-term follow-up care.
ai.summary: The AYA TEAMS study enrolled 587 survivors aged 16–25 from three pediatric oncology centres and followed them for at least two years. It collected information on self-management, transition readiness, family factors, and engagement in long-term follow-up care through surveys and medical records.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps researchers understand what supports young people in staying engaged with recommended cancer follow-up care as they move into adulthood.
ai.life_skill: Notice what helps you keep track of your own health appointments and information as you get older.
ai.fact: The cohort included 587 adolescent and young adult survivors of childhood cancer, with an average age of 19.7 years.

quiz.question: What type of study is AYA TEAMS?
quiz.answer: It is a longitudinal observational cohort study.

ai.caveat: As an observational study, it can show links but cannot prove what causes better self-management or engagement in care.

items.title: Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics

ai.headline: AI agents can now write and improve computer graphics code, creating a new way to make graphics automatically.
ai.summary: This preprint reviews research on agentic computer graphics, where large language model agents generate graphics code and refine it using feedback. The authors introduce a unified taxonomy to describe these systems and a tool to help researchers analyse papers at scale.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI is changing creative and technical work, which may affect how graphics are made in games, design and everyday software.
ai.life_skill: Notice when AI tools help create or edit digital images or code, and check their output carefully before relying on it.
ai.fact: Large language model agents can generate graphics code and iteratively refine it through feedback.

quiz.question: What can LLM agents do in agentic computer graphics according to the abstract?
quiz.answer: They can generate graphics code and iteratively refine it through various feedback.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and is a review of existing research rather than new experimental evidence.

items.title: Doctor ȷobs in illegal Israeli settlements advertised at “obscene” London event

ai.headline: Medical jobs in Israeli settlements were advertised to UK doctors at a London jobs fair.
ai.summary: The BMJ reports that leaflets advertising medical jobs in illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank were distributed at a London recruitment event attended by over 130 British doctors. Medical charities have condemned the event as obscene, coming shortly after the UK government tightened its stance on settlements.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how international political disagreements can appear in everyday settings such as job fairs in the UK.
ai.life_skill: Check where a job is based before applying, especially if the employer operates in disputed territory.
ai.fact: The UK government has announced a ban on imports from Israeli settlements and restrictions on those who finance or facilitate them.

quiz.question: Where were medical jobs in Israeli settlements advertised to UK doctors?
quiz.answer: At a London jobs fair called MedEx.

ai.caveat: This is a single news report, not peer-reviewed research, so the claims should be treated as allegations rather than established findings.

items.title: NASA's Hubble and Webb discover ancient worlds that remember their past

ai.headline: Telescopes found 27 ancient objects beyond Neptune that have barely changed since the solar system formed.
ai.summary: Researchers used the Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes to study 27 small, distant objects beyond Neptune. They found these ancient building blocks of planets have stayed remarkably unchanged for billions of years, though their sizes and numbers challenge current ideas about how planets form.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps us understand how our solar system and planet came to be.
ai.fact: 27 distant objects beyond Neptune have remained largely unchanged for billions of years.

quiz.question: What did scientists find about the 27 distant objects beyond Neptune?
quiz.answer: They have remained remarkably unchanged for billions of years.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising research, not the original peer-reviewed study, so details are limited.

items.title: Can Home Visits Re-Engage Chronically Absent Students? Evidence from the LEAP Program -- by Eric Brunner, Shangyue Jiang, Stephen Ross

ai.headline: Home visits by school staff helped chronically absent students attend more and behave better.
ai.summary: Researchers studied Connecticut’s LEAP programme, which sent school staff to visit students who were chronically absent and their families. Students who received home visits attended school about 4 to 5 percentage points more, were 13 to 15 percentage points less likely to be chronically absent, and had 3 to 5 percentage points fewer disciplinary incidents.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a practical way schools can rebuild connections with students who have disengaged from education.
ai.life_skill: Try reaching out to a trusted teacher or school staff member if you are struggling to attend school regularly.
ai.fact: Home visits by school personnel are linked to improved attendance and fewer disciplinary incidents among chronically absent students.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the study is observational rather than a randomised trial, so it cannot prove the home visits caused the improvements.

items.title: Can Australia's social welfare system handle future aged care needs?

ai.headline: Most older Australians applying for aged care rely on social welfare payments.
ai.summary: Researchers studied more than 920,000 older people, average age 82, who applied for aged care in Australia between 2010 and 2019. They found that nine in ten applicants received social welfare payments, highlighting the financial circumstances and income sources of this group.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how much the aged care system depends on social welfare as the population ages.
ai.life_skill: Check what government support you or a relative might qualify for before needing aged care.
ai.fact: Nine in ten older Australians applying for aged care receive social welfare payments.

quiz.question: What share of older Australians applying for aged care receive social welfare payments?
quiz.answer: Nine in ten applicants receive social welfare payments.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study based on applications from 2010 to 2019, so it cannot prove cause and effect or predict future system capacity.

items.title: Meet Neuropixels: how probes that track hundreds of brain cells at once are revolutionizing neuroscience

ai.headline: New brain probes can record hundreds of neurons at once, revealing how brains work.
ai.summary: The article describes Neuropixels probes, which track hundreds of brain cells simultaneously in rodents and humans. These tools are exposing the inner workings of the brain by enabling large-scale, single-cell neuronal recordings.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how new technology is helping scientists understand the brain, which underlies how we think, feel and behave.
ai.fact: Neuropixels probes can record from hundreds of individual brain cells at the same time.

quiz.question: What do Neuropixels probes enable scientists to do?
quiz.answer: They enable large-scale, single-cell neuronal recordings by tracking hundreds of brain cells at once.

ai.caveat: This is a news article describing a technology, not a research study with tested results.

items.title: [Articles] Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study
authors: Yasaman Vali, Kristy Wonders, Jenny Lee, Guruprasad P Aithal, Rocio Aller, Michael E D Allison, Johanna Arola, Jesus M Banales, Vanesa Bernal-Monterde, Annalisa Berzigotti, Jérôme Boursier, Clifford A Brass, Elisabetta Bugianesi, Jose Luis Calleja, Jeremy F Cobbold, Helena Cortez-Pinto, Javier Crespo, Susan Davies, Ann Driessen, Kevin L Duffin, Mattias Ekstedt, Daniel Forton, Céline Fournier-Poizat, Sven Francque, Andreas Geier, Joseph Gogain, Annette S H Gouw, Hannes Hagström, Adriaan G Holleboom, Prodromos Hytiroglou, Morten Karsdal, Carolin Lackner, Diana J Leeming, Luca Miele, George Papatheodoridis, Valerie Paradis, Michael Pavlides, Juan M Pericàs, Salvatore Petta, Vlad Ratziu, Manuel Romero-Gomez, Jörn M Schattenberg, Detlef Schuppan, Rambabu Surabattula, Ana Paula Silva, Mette Skalshøi Kjær, Beate K Straub, Gianluca Svegliati-Baroni, Dina Tiniakos, Maria Manuela Tonini, Richard Torstenson, Luca V C Valenti, Joanne Verheij, Jeremy Magnanensi, Rebeca Mayo, David Wenn, Hannele Yki-Järvinen, Carla Yunis, Patrick M Bossuyt, Quentin M Anstee, LITMUS Investigators

ai.headline: A combination of blood tests may spot serious fatty liver disease better than single markers.
ai.summary: Researchers compared non-invasive tests with liver biopsy for detecting at-risk MASH in people with MASLD. Single markers performed poorly, but multimarker panels—especially a proteomic panel—showed strong diagnostic potential.
ai.why_it_matters: Better non-invasive tests could mean fewer liver biopsies and earlier identification of people who need care.
ai.life_skill: Ask a qualified healthcare professional which tests are appropriate if you are concerned about liver health.
ai.fact: Single markers had variable and limited performance compared with histology for detecting at-risk MASH.

quiz.question: How did multimarker panels compare with single markers for detecting at-risk MASH?
quiz.answer: Multimarker panels showed strong diagnostic performance, while single markers were variable and limited.

ai.caveat: This is one prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study, so the findings need confirmation before changing guidelines or practice.

items.title: Fire losses to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060 without new protections

ai.headline: Without new protections, fire damage to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060.
ai.summary: Researchers studied how climate change, vegetation management and building practices affect fire risk to structures in the United States. They found that if no action is taken, the risk to buildings could almost triple by midcentury.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how choices about where and how we build can shape future danger from fires.
ai.life_skill: Check whether your home is in a fire-prone area and learn basic fire-safety steps.
ai.fact: Fires in the U.S. are getting faster, larger and more dangerous.

quiz.question: What could happen to fire risk for U.S. buildings by 2060 if no new protections are put in place?
quiz.answer: It could nearly triple.

ai.caveat: This is a projection based on a model, not a certainty, and depends on future actions and conditions.

items.title: We are finally pinning down what makes dyslexic brains different

ai.headline: Researchers are identifying the specific brain pathways that distinguish dyslexia from typical reading development.
ai.summary: This news report highlights that humans did not evolve to read, yet about 10% of people have dyslexia. Scientists are currently uncovering the underlying neural pathways of the condition, which could lead to better support for those who struggle with reading.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the biological basis of dyslexia helps reduce stigma and guides the development of more effective educational strategies.
ai.life_skill: Notice that reading difficulties are often linked to specific brain pathways rather than a lack of effort or intelligence.
ai.fact: Approximately 10 per cent of the human population is dyslexic.

quiz.question: What percentage of people are estimated to be dyslexic?
quiz.answer: Around 10 per cent of people are dyslexic.

ai.caveat: This is a news summary rather than a primary research paper, so it lacks specific details on the study design, sample size, or exact findings.

items.title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

ai.headline: The UK government is launching its first study to measure PFAS chemicals in people's bodies.
ai.summary: A major UK study will measure levels of PFAS, known as 'forever chemicals', in the population to understand potential health risks.
ai.why_it_matters: PFAS are widespread in everyday products and the environment, so knowing how much is in people's bodies helps assess public health risks.
ai.life_skill: Check whether everyday products you use contain PFAS and look for PFAS-free alternatives where possible.
ai.fact: PFAS are called 'forever chemicals' because they break down very slowly in the environment and can build up in people's bodies.

quiz.question: What is the UK government launching its first study to measure in people's bodies?
quiz.answer: The study will measure levels of PFAS chemicals in the UK population.

ai.caveat: This is a news announcement about a planned study, not peer-reviewed research with findings yet.

items.title: Predictive modelling approaches for childhood diarrhoeal disease: a systematic review (2000-2025).

ai.headline: Most prediction models for childhood diarrhoea lack strong validation and are not yet ready for real-world use.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 38 studies published between 2000 and 2025 that used statistical, machine learning or hybrid models to predict childhood diarrhoea. They found that five of the 15 individual-level models had a high overall risk of bias, and only three of the 19 population-level forecasting studies used rigorous out-of-sample temporal validation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that tools meant to warn about childhood diarrhoea are often not yet reliable enough to guide decisions or policies.
ai.life_skill: Check whether a health prediction tool has been tested on new data before trusting its warnings.
ai.fact: Childhood diarrhoeal disease remains a leading cause of child mortality worldwide.

quiz.question: How many of the 19 population-level forecasting studies used rigorous out-of-sample temporal validation?
quiz.answer: Only three of the 19 studies undertook rigorous out-of-sample temporal validation.

ai.caveat: This is a systematic review of modelling studies, so it appraises existing research rather than proving that any particular model works in practice.

items.title: Deep reinforcement learning based personalized mathematics learning path planning algorithm for children

ai.headline: A computer model used AI to personalise maths lessons for young children and scored highly in tests.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a Learning-Based Q Network that adapts maths learning paths to children’s cognitive and behavioural states using a dataset of 4,000 rows. It outperformed three existing methods, reaching 93.8% accuracy, 90.6% recall, 91.7% F1-score, and a 4.9 out of 5 user-satisfaction rating.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how adaptive digital tools might one day tailor early maths teaching to individual learners.

quiz.question: What accuracy did the LBQN model achieve?
quiz.answer: It achieved an accuracy of 93.8%.

ai.caveat: This is a single modelling study using one dataset, not proof that the system works in real classrooms with actual children.

items.title: Trust in AI: A Decision-Theoretic framework for Human–AI Interactions in the Digital Society

ai.headline: Trust in AI can be understood as a decision to weigh risks and rewards before following AI advice.
ai.summary: This paper proposes a decision-theoretic framework for human–AI trust. It suggests that trusting AI means choosing to delegate control by balancing potential rewards and risks against using one’s own judgment, and that theories such as Prospect Theory, Evidence Accumulation Models, and Reinforcement Learning can explain how people evaluate AI advice and update trust from feedback.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a way to think about when to rely on AI tools in everyday decisions such as health, finance, or work.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you are about to follow AI advice and pause to weigh the possible benefits and risks yourself.
ai.fact: Trust in AI can be framed as a decision to delegate control to an artificial agent.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint proposing a framework, not peer-reviewed evidence from an experiment.

items.title: The effects of Tai Chi on executive function and neurophysiological outcomes in college students: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

ai.headline: Tai Chi may briefly improve inhibitory control in college students, but broader benefits are unproven.
ai.summary: A systematic review of seven randomised trials involving 425 university students looked at Tai Chi and executive function. It found a possible short-term improvement in inhibitory control, but evidence for working memory, cognitive flexibility and academic outcomes was weak or absent.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a low-cost activity might help a specific thinking skill, but stronger evidence is needed before it can be recommended as a reliable study aid.
ai.life_skill: Try practising Tai Chi regularly if you enjoy it, but do not rely on it alone to improve your focus or exam performance.
ai.fact: Tai Chi combines physical movement, motor-sequence learning, postural control, breathing regulation and sustained attention.

quiz.question: What did the review find about Tai Chi and inhibitory control in college students?
quiz.answer: It found a possible short-term improvement in inhibitory-control performance, though the certainty of the evidence was low.

ai.caveat: The main result was driven by one trial, was not robust under a different statistical analysis, and the evidence certainty was low.

items.title: Efficacy of animal-assisted therapy for the relief of dental anxiety: quantitative synthesis of clinical randomized controlled trial evidence

ai.headline: Dog-assisted therapy may reduce dental anxiety, especially in children, but evidence is weak.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 10 randomised trials with 524 patients found dog-mediated animal-assisted therapy linked to lower dental anxiety than control conditions, along with better behaviour, pain perception and physiological indicators. Effects were stronger in children, while adults showed limited improvement in objective anxiety measures despite higher satisfaction.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible low-cost way to make dental visits less stressful, particularly for children, though the evidence is not yet certain.
ai.life_skill: Ask your dentist whether a calm, trained dog could be present during your appointment if you feel anxious.
ai.fact: Dog-mediated animal-assisted therapy was linked to reduced dental anxiety compared with control conditions in the reviewed trials.

quiz.question: What did the review find about dog-mediated animal-assisted therapy and dental anxiety?
quiz.answer: It was associated with reduced dental anxiety compared with control conditions, though the evidence was rated as very low certainty.

ai.caveat: The evidence is very low certainty with high heterogeneity across studies, so the findings should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: Nutrition and Mental Health in Endocrine Disorders with a Focus on Depression and Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review
items.venue: Iranian Journal of Diabetes and Metabolism

ai.headline: Better nutrition and healthy eating patterns may help reduce depressive symptoms in people with endocrine disorders such as diabetes and PCOS.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 38 studies on nutrition and depression in people with endocrine disorders like diabetes, thyroid dysfunction and PCOS. It found that vitamin D supplements were linked to fewer depressive symptoms in some trials, while healthier diets and plant-based foods were linked to lower depressive symptoms, whereas ultra-processed foods and food insecurity were linked to higher risk. Evidence for omega-3 fatty acids was mixed and thyroid disorders were under-studied.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that everyday food choices may be connected to mental wellbeing for people living with common hormone conditions.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different eating patterns affect your mood and discuss any dietary changes with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Endocrine disorders such as diabetes, thyroid dysfunction and PCOS are associated with an increased risk of depression.

quiz.question: What did the review find about ultra-processed foods and food insecurity in type 2 diabetes?
quiz.answer: They were associated with a higher risk of depression.

ai.caveat: The included studies varied widely and the authors call for larger, well-designed trials, so the findings are not yet proof.

items.title: Depressive symptoms and incident chronic lung disease: a three- cohort cross-national comparison of 117,160 adults from China, the United States, and Europe

ai.headline: Depressive symptoms are linked to a higher risk of developing chronic lung disease across China, the US and Europe.
ai.summary: Researchers followed 117,160 adults without chronic lung disease in three national cohorts. Baseline depressive symptoms were linked to about a 50% higher risk of developing chronic lung disease, with persistently high symptoms linked to the greatest risk.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests mental health may be connected to future physical health, not just the other way around.
ai.life_skill: Notice persistent low mood or physical symptoms of depression and consider speaking with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Both somatic and cognitive-affective depressive symptoms were independently linked to incident chronic lung disease.

quiz.question: What was the pooled hazard ratio for incident chronic lung disease associated with baseline depressive symptoms?
quiz.answer: The pooled hazard ratio was 1.54, meaning about a 54% higher risk.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the study design cannot prove that depressive symptoms cause chronic lung disease.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of bereavement-related distress: a systematic review

ai.headline: Medicines do not appear to reduce grief symptoms, though some may help depression after bereavement.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 33 studies involving 211,920 bereaved people to see if medication helps grief-related distress. It found no evidence that any medication reduced grief symptoms across controlled studies, while antidepressants and a beta blocker plus aspirin appeared to help depression symptoms in bereaved individuals.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that medication is not currently proven to treat prolonged grief, so people struggling after a bereavement should look beyond drugs for support.
ai.life_skill: If you are struggling with grief, speak to a GP or a qualified bereavement counsellor about non-medication support options.
ai.fact: Prolonged grief disorder is included in both the DSM-5-TR and ICD-11 diagnostic manuals.

quiz.question: Did the review find that medication reduced grief symptoms in controlled studies?
quiz.answer: No, no medications reduced grief symptomatology across any controlled studies.

ai.caveat: The included studies were of low quality and reported data inconsistently, so the findings are not definitive.

items.title: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with amyloid accumulation over 3 years in cognitively healthy adults

ai.headline: Repetitive negative thinking is linked to faster amyloid build-up in the brain over three years.

ai.summary: Researchers studied how high-cholesterol diets can weaken the body's natural cholesterol defences. In mice, blocking this hidden mechanism dramatically lowered harmful LDL cholesterol. An experimental drug targeting the same pathway has passed an early human safety trial.
ai.why_it_matters: It points to a possible new cholesterol treatment, but the human evidence is only an early safety trial so far.
ai.fact: High-cholesterol diets can undermine the body's natural cholesterol defences in mice.

quiz.question: What did blocking the hidden mechanism do to harmful LDL cholesterol in mice?
quiz.answer: It dramatically lowered it.

ai.caveat: The cholesterol-lowering effect was demonstrated in mice, and the human trial only assessed early safety, so it is not yet proof for people generally.

items.title: Dose-Dependent Effect of Crocin on Depressive and Anxiety Symptom Scores: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

ai.headline: Crocin reduces depression and anxiety
ai.summary: Researchers studied the effect of crocin on depression and anxiety symptoms. They found that crocin supplementation can improve symptom scores in a dose-response manner. The study included 14 randomized controlled trials.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it could lead to new treatments for depression and anxiety
ai.life_skill: Try consulting a healthcare professional about crocin supplementation
ai.fact: Crocin supplementation is linked to improved depression and anxiety symptom scores

quiz.question: What is the effect of crocin on depressive symptoms?
quiz.answer: Crocin supplementation can decrease depressive symptom scores

ai.caveat: The results are based on clinical trials with relatively small sample sizes and mostly conducted in one country

items.title: Global Preferences and Determinant Variables of Caesarean Delivery Among Pregnant Women: A systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Caesarean delivery preferred by 26% globally
ai.summary: Researchers studied global preferences for caesarean delivery among pregnant women. They found that 26% of women preferred caesarean delivery and identified factors associated with this preference. These factors included age, education, and prior pregnancy complications.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the factors that influence women's preferences for caesarean delivery can inform healthcare policies and improve maternal care.
ai.life_skill: Check your healthcare provider's guidance on delivery options
ai.fact: Globally, 26% of pregnant women prefer caesarean delivery

quiz.question: What percentage of pregnant women globally prefer caesarean delivery?
quiz.answer: 26% of pregnant women globally prefer caesarean delivery

ai.caveat: The study's findings may not be generalizable to all populations due to variations in healthcare systems and cultural contexts.

items.title: Postnatal Care Service Provision, Uptake among Women, and Stakeholder Perceptions in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

ai.headline: Postnatal care uptake is inconsistent
ai.summary: Researchers studied postnatal care provision and uptake in sub-Saharan Africa. They found that despite high service availability, uptake was only 42%. Providers and women identified several barriers to utilisation, including inadequate staffing and limited knowledge.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because improving postnatal care uptake can help prevent avoidable deaths and promote maternal and newborn wellbeing
ai.life_skill: Check that your local healthcare services provide respectful and accessible postnatal care
ai.fact: Postnatal care service availability in sub-Saharan Africa ranges from 85.4% to 97.6%

quiz.question: What was the pooled uptake of postnatal care among women in the study?
quiz.answer: The pooled uptake of postnatal care was 42%

ai.caveat: The review was limited to English language studies published between 2016 and 2026

items.title: Cognitive Control as a Brake on the Depression–Internet Addiction Link: Task-Based fMRI Evidence from Activation and Task-Modulated Functional Connectivity

ai.headline: Cognitive control affects depression-Internet link
ai.summary: This study examined the relationship between depressive symptoms, Internet addiction, and cognitive control using fMRI. It found that cognitive control-related brain activation and functional connectivity moderate this association. The findings suggest that certain brain regions may buffer or amplify the depression-Internet addiction link.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding this relationship can help develop strategies to mitigate Internet addiction in individuals with depressive symptoms
ai.life_skill: Try to practice self-control when using the internet
ai.fact: Cognitive control is linked to the relationship between depressive symptoms and Internet addiction

quiz.question: What type of brain activation was studied in relation to Internet addiction?
quiz.answer: Cognitive control-related brain activation

ai.caveat: The study is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution

items.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practices towards anthrax among Communities in the Southern and South-western Ethiopia

ai.headline: In rural Ethiopia, many people know about anthrax but still handle dead animals unsafely.
ai.summary: This cross-sectional study interviewed 382 household heads in southern and southwestern Ethiopia about their knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding anthrax. While most participants had adequate knowledge and a positive attitude toward the disease, only about half reported good prevention practices, with some still sharing or eating meat from animals that died suddenly.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that knowing about a disease is not enough; safe habits, like not eating meat from unexplained animal deaths, are crucial to prevent zoonotic infections.
ai.life_skill: Notice that if an animal dies suddenly without a clear cause, avoid handling or consuming its meat and report it to local authorities.
ai.fact: Anthrax is a zoonotic disease caused by Bacillus anthracis that affects both livestock and humans.

quiz.question: What was the most common unsafe practice reported regarding dead animals?
quiz.answer: Sharing and eating the meat with the community and family was reported by 10.7% of respondents.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional study in specific Ethiopian districts, so results may not apply to other regions or populations.

items.title: Enablers and barriers to scaling an ECD parenting program into primary health care services in rural Bangladesh

ai.headline: Strong government support helps parenting programs work in rural Bangladesh clinics.
ai.summary: This study looked at how a parenting program for young children was integrated into rural health clinics in Bangladesh. It found that government ownership and high compliance by health workers were key strengths, while poor supervision and lack of play materials were major barriers.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that for public health programs to succeed, they need clear leadership and consistent support, not just good intentions.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the people responsible for a group project have clear support and resources, as this predicts success.
ai.fact: In rural Bangladesh, community health workers delivered parenting sessions fortnightly for one year to mothers of malnourished children.

quiz.question: What was identified as a key barrier to the program's success?
quiz.answer: Low levels of supervision and poor communication across health staff were key barriers.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not final.

items.title: The generative paradox: the Anti-Prompt paradigm for human capability

ai.headline: AI should help people keep their own skills, not just produce better results together.
ai.summary: The paper argues that judging AI only by joint human-AI output misses whether people can still understand, challenge, repair and adapt work when AI support changes or disappears. It calls this tension the generative paradox and proposes an Anti-Prompt approach where AI first creates conditions for human construction instead of generating immediately.
ai.why_it_matters: It matters because relying on AI for answers can quietly erode the very skills people need to work independently later.
ai.life_skill: Try solving a problem yourself before asking AI for help, so you keep your own understanding and ability to adapt.
ai.fact: Judging AI only by joint human-AI output can overlook whether people retain the ability to understand, challenge, repair and adapt work when support changes or disappears.

quiz.question: What does the Anti-Prompt paradigm do differently?
quiz.answer: It reverses the usual order so AI first creates conditions for human construction instead of generating immediately.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and presents a conceptual proposal rather than tested evidence.

items.title: Salience network expansion as a transdiagnostic neural marker for psychopathology risk in adolescence

ai.headline: A larger brain salience network in early adolescence is linked to general mental health difficulties rather than depression alone.
ai.summary: Researchers looked at brain scans and behaviour reports from thousands of children aged 9–12. A larger salience network was modestly linked to depressive symptoms at first, but this did not repeat two years later; instead, it was linked to overall mental health problems at both time points.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests brain network differences may reflect broad mental health risk rather than one specific condition, which could shape how we understand adolescent wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice changes in your mood or behaviour and talk to a trusted adult or professional if you are concerned.
ai.fact: The salience network is a brain system involved in detecting important information and switching between other brain networks.

quiz.question: Did the link between a larger salience network and depressive symptoms repeat two years later?
quiz.answer: No, that association did not replicate in the second sample.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the study only shows links, not causes.

items.title: Making argumentative work visible in GenAI-mediated assessment: an exploratory LLM simulation and questionnaire study in university ideological and political education

ai.headline: Structured writing tasks and clear AI rules can make student thinking more visible than free-form essays.
ai.summary: The study tested three university assignment formats and three AI-use scenarios using simulated texts and student evaluations. Tasks that required students to explain sources, respond to objections, and show revisions scored higher and showed clearer thinking than simple position essays, especially when AI use was open and responsible.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how course design can reveal whether students are actually thinking through arguments or just handing in polished AI-generated text.
ai.life_skill: When writing an assignment, note down where each idea came from, address a strong objection, and explain what you changed and why.
ai.fact: Open-ended responses linked evidence integration, comparing reasons, and revision with thinking, while formulaic structure and over-polished expression were seen as signs of AI-like writing.

quiz.question: Which assignment format scored highest for source–claim linkage in the questionnaire?
quiz.answer: Evidence-integration memoranda were rated highest for source–claim linkage.

ai.caveat: The findings come from an LLM simulation and questionnaire, not from observing real students completing real assignments, so they may not reflect actual classroom behaviour.

items.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes

ai.headline: Chemists built an AI tool designed to help scientists create better enzymes rather than replace them.
ai.summary: Researchers developed an artificial intelligence tool intended to support scientists in designing life-enhancing enzymes. The goal is to elevate human scientific work instead of replacing researchers.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI might be used as a helper in science rather than as a replacement for human expertise.
ai.life_skill: Notice how AI tools can assist human work instead of assuming they will replace people.
ai.fact: An AI tool has been created to support scientists in designing enzymes.
ai.caveat: This is a news report about research, not the full study, so details and findings are limited.

items.title: [Comment] Offline: Seizing new opportunities for climate and health

ai.headline: A major health report now frames climate change as a global health opportunity rather than just a threat.
ai.summary: This commentary marks the tenth anniversary of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change. It notes a shift in perspective from a 2009 Commission that called climate change the greatest threat to health, to a 2025 Commission describing it as the greatest opportunity for global health.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how society’s view of climate change is evolving from pure fear to a chance for positive change, which can influence how people engage with environmental issues.
ai.life_skill: Notice how framing a problem as an opportunity rather than a threat can change your motivation to act.
ai.fact: The Lancet Commission on climate change and health in 2025 described climate change as the greatest opportunity for global health in the 21st century.

quiz.question: How did the 2025 Lancet Commission describe climate change?
quiz.answer: It described climate change as the greatest opportunity for global health in the 21st century.

ai.caveat: This is a commentary piece reflecting institutional perspectives and anniversaries, not new empirical research or data.

items.title: Twin study links artistic, but not scientific, creativity to poorer mental health

ai.headline: Artistic creativity is linked to poorer mental health, but scientific creativity is not.
ai.summary: A twin study examined the relationship between creativity and mental health. It found that artistic creativity was linked to poorer mental health, while scientific creativity was not.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that different types of creativity may have different relationships with mental wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether creative hobbies affect your mood and seek professional support if they cause distress.
ai.fact: Artistic creativity is linked to poorer mental health, whereas scientific creativity is not.

quiz.question: Which type of creativity was linked to poorer mental health in the study?
quiz.answer: Artistic creativity was linked to poorer mental health, but scientific creativity was not.

ai.caveat: A single observational study cannot prove that artistic creativity causes poorer mental health.

items.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions

ai.headline: A new computer method inserts objects into photos so they look physically realistic in light and position.
ai.summary: PhysInsert is a framework that adapts objects and scenes together so inserted objects match lighting, perspective and pose. It uses a new dataset of aligned rendered image pairs and benchmarks to test insertion across different environments and viewpoints. Tests and a user study found better image fidelity and more plausible placement and lighting integration.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI-generated image editing is being made more physically believable, which matters as edited photos become more common online.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether lighting and shadows match when you see an object placed into a photo online.
ai.fact: PhysInsert is a preprint on arXiv and has not yet been peer reviewed.

quiz.question: What does PhysInsert aim to make inserted objects match in a new scene?
quiz.answer: It aims to match lighting, perspective and pose so the insertion looks physically plausible.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the evidence comes from benchmarks and a user study rather than independent confirmation.

items.title: Facilitating Advance Care Planning Discussions for People With Advanced Cancer

ai.headline: Researchers are testing a web-based tool to help people with advanced cancer plan future care with family.
ai.summary: The study looks at how 20 patient–family pairs make advance care planning decisions and tests a web-based resilience-building intervention with 9 pairs to improve its content and design.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how researchers develop digital tools to support difficult conversations about future medical care.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you might want to talk with family about your future healthcare wishes.
ai.fact: Advance care planning involves patients and family caregivers discussing future treatment preferences together.

quiz.question: How many patient–family pairs were involved in the usability testing?
quiz.answer: Nine dyads took part in the usability testing to refine the web-based intervention.

ai.caveat: This is a small trial with only 29 dyads total and results are newly posted, so findings are preliminary.

items.title: Even stupendous black holes can’t explain dark matter

ai.headline: Huge black holes probably cannot explain dark matter because they would leave a bigger mark on cosmic radiation.
ai.summary: The article examines theoretical objects called stupendous black holes as a possible source of dark matter. It finds that if they were responsible for the invisible force holding galaxies together, they would have left a larger imprint on cosmic radiation than observed.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps narrow down what dark matter might be, advancing our understanding of how the universe is structured.
ai.fact: Dark matter is the invisible force thought to pull galaxies together.

quiz.question: Why can’t stupendous black holes explain dark matter according to the article?
quiz.answer: Because they would have left a larger imprint on cosmic radiation if they were the source of dark matter.

ai.caveat: This is a short Nature news item based on theoretical reasoning, not new experimental proof.

items.title: Scientists discover a bacterial defense so strange they thought it was broken

ai.headline: Scientists found a bacterial defense that waits for infection before making its lethal weapon and kills itself to stop viruses spreading.
ai.summary: Researchers studied an unusual bacterial immune system. Unlike typical defenses that keep a toxin ready, this one only produces its weapon after a virus infects the cell, causing the bacterium to destroy itself and block the virus from spreading to neighbors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a surprising way living things can protect a group by sacrificing themselves, helping us understand how bacteria and viruses interact in nature.
ai.fact: Some bacteria defend against viruses by destroying themselves after infection to stop the virus spreading to nearby cells.

quiz.question: What does the unusual bacterial defense do after a virus infects the cell?
quiz.answer: It produces its lethal weapon and destroys itself to stop the virus multiplying and spreading.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the original peer-reviewed research, so the details have not been independently verified.

items.title: Fish pay attention to one influential neighbour in virtual reality

ai.headline: Each fish in a group follows cues from just one influential neighbour.
ai.summary: Researchers observed real rummy-nose tetra fish interacting with virtual fish in virtual reality. They found that within a group, each individual takes cues from only one influential neighbour.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how simple local rules can shape group behaviour in animals and possibly in human crowds too.
ai.life_skill: Notice who you tend to follow in a group and check whether they are actually worth listening to.
ai.fact: Rummy-nose tetra fish take social cues from only one influential neighbour within a group.

quiz.question: How many influential neighbours does each fish take cues from?
quiz.answer: Each individual takes cues from only one influential neighbour.

ai.caveat: This is a single news report of a study, not peer-reviewed research, so the finding should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'

ai.headline: Oil tank vandalism has polluted a waterfowl park pond, forcing it to close.
ai.summary: Vandals damaged an oil tank, causing oil to enter a pond at a popular attraction in County Down. The park has been forced to close while workers remove the oil from the water.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how damage to infrastructure can harm local wildlife spaces and disrupt public access.
ai.life_skill: Report suspected pollution or environmental damage to the relevant authority promptly.
ai.fact: Oil contamination can force the temporary closure of a public waterfowl park.

quiz.question: Why has the County Down waterfowl park closed?
quiz.answer: Because oil from a vandalised tank entered the pond and is being removed.

ai.caveat: This is a single news report with no data, methods, or independent verification.

items.title: Whole-brain mapping of spinal-projecting neurons in larval zebrafish

ai.headline: Scientists mapped all brain cells that send movement commands to the spinal cord in young zebrafish.
ai.summary: The study used a light-activated marker in transparent larval zebrafish to create a whole-brain map of spinal-projecting neurons. It found far more of these neurons than previously known, spread across the hindbrain, midbrain, and diencephalon.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps scientists understand how brains across vertebrates, including humans, organise movement commands.
ai.fact: Zebrafish have spinal-projecting neurons distributed across the hindbrain, midbrain, and diencephalic structures.

quiz.question: What did the researchers map in larval zebrafish?
quiz.answer: They mapped all neurons sending axons toward the spinal cord.

ai.caveat: The findings are from larval zebrafish, so they may not directly apply to humans or other species.

items.title: An LLM Workflow for Functional Form Sensitivity Analysis -- by Isaiah Andrews, Simon C. Essig Aberg, Jesse M. Shapiro

ai.headline: An AI workflow can test how much a research estimate changes when the assumed mathematical shape is altered.
ai.summary: The paper describes a workflow using large language models to check how sensitive a research estimate is to the choice of functional form. It finds an analytic solution where possible, otherwise uses numerical methods, and provides a verifiable lower bound on sensitivity. It is illustrated using the welfare cost of adverse selection in health insurance.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps readers understand that research conclusions can depend on arbitrary mathematical assumptions, not just the data.
ai.life_skill: Check whether a reported estimate changes when a different mathematical assumption is used.
ai.fact: Sensitivity can be measured by how much an estimate changes without compromising model fit when a different functional form is selected.

quiz.question: What does the workflow provide a verifiable lower bound on?
quiz.answer: It provides a verifiable lower bound on the in-sample sensitivity of the researcher’s estimate.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and illustrates a methodological workflow rather than establishing a causal finding.

items.title: Scientists finally discover how a common gut bacterium can trigger colon cancer

ai.headline: A common gut bacterium’s toxin can damage the colon lining, cause inflammation, and promote tumour formation.
ai.summary: Researchers studied Bacteroides fragilis, a common gut bacterium. They found its toxin damages the colon’s protective lining, triggers chronic inflammation, and promotes tumour formation.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how gut bacteria may contribute to colorectal cancer, which could inform future prevention and treatment research.
ai.fact: Bacteroides fragilis produces a toxin linked to colon lining damage, chronic inflammation, and tumour formation.

quiz.question: What does the toxin from Bacteroides fragilis do according to the study?
quiz.answer: It damages the colon’s protective lining, triggers chronic inflammation, and promotes tumour formation.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising research, not the original peer-reviewed study, so details and certainty are limited.

items.title: Venlafaxine in oncology: supportive-care evidence and emerging preclinical anticancer signals: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Venlafaxine may help cancer-related hot flashes, but there is no proof it treats cancer itself.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 25 studies looked at venlafaxine in oncology. It found the strongest evidence for reducing treatment-related hot flashes, especially in breast cancer survivors on endocrine therapy, while evidence for nerve pain and other symptoms was limited or inconsistent. Preclinical hints of anticancer effects exist only in lab models and are not proven in people.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows where current evidence stands for a medicine sometimes used in cancer care and reminds us that lab results do not equal proven treatments.
ai.life_skill: Talk to your oncology team before using venlafaxine for any symptom, and do not assume it treats cancer.
ai.fact: The strongest clinical evidence supported venlafaxine for treatment-related hot flashes, particularly among breast cancer survivors receiving endocrine therapy.

quiz.question: Does the review provide clinical evidence that venlafaxine directly treats cancer?
quiz.answer: No, the review states no clinical evidence currently supports venlafaxine as a direct anticancer treatment.

ai.caveat: The anticancer findings come from only two preclinical studies and are hypothesis-generating, not proof in humans.

items.title: Improving Female Health at Various Life Stages: A systematic review of the impact of date fruit products

ai.headline: Date fruit products may support female health from puberty through menopause, according to a review of 21 studies.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 21 studies on date fruit products and female health across life stages. It found links between date fruit intake and better hemoglobin levels in adolescent girls, improved fertility parameters and sexual function in reproductive-age women, and reduced dyspareunia plus ovarian reserve support in menopause.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a simple, low-cost food choice could support women’s wellbeing at different stages of life.
ai.life_skill: Try including date fruits as part of a varied, balanced diet.
ai.fact: Date fruit consumption was associated with improved hemoglobin levels in adolescent girls in the reviewed studies.

quiz.question: What did the review find about date fruit intake in adolescent girls?
quiz.answer: It was associated with improved hemoglobin levels.

ai.caveat: The review combines observational findings of varying quality, so it shows links rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Motivators and barriers to physical activity: a systematic review of qualitative studies
items.venue: International Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health

ai.headline: People are more active when they feel supported, have flexible routines, and live in safe, walkable places.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at nine qualitative studies on what helps and stops adults from being physically active. It found motivators such as health benefits, social support, flexible programmes, and walkable neighbourhoods, and barriers such as fatigue, lack of support, workload, and unsafe surroundings.
ai.why_it_matters: Knowing these common motivators and barriers can help people and communities make physical activity easier to fit into daily life.
ai.life_skill: Try making your activity routine flexible and ask a friend or family member to support you.
ai.fact: Physical activity is linked to better mental and physical health.

quiz.question: What did the review identify as a key motivator for physical activity?
quiz.answer: Social support from family, peers, and instructors was a principal motivator.

ai.caveat: The review included only nine English-language qualitative studies, so the findings may not apply to all groups or settings.

items.title: NICE’s 2026 Consultation Draft Guideline for OCD and BDD (GID-NG10435): A Critical Appraisal with Secondary Analysis of NICE’s Published Data

ai.headline: A draft UK guideline for OCD and BDD has gaps in its evidence and missing treatment details.
ai.summary: Researchers appraised NICE’s 2026 draft guideline update for obsessive-compulsive disorder and body dysmorphic disorder. They found that some treatments were not recommended because of small samples and uncertain results, while others were recommended despite similar limitations, and several practical treatment details are not specified.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how health guidelines are built from evidence and where important questions may still be unanswered.
ai.life_skill: Check that any treatment advice you follow is based on clear, specific guidance from a qualified professional.
ai.fact: The draft OCD review included 82 randomised controlled trials and the BDD review included 13 studies.

quiz.question: What did the researchers say about the draft guideline’s rationale for recommending some treatments but not others?
quiz.answer: It does not fully explain why small samples and imprecision precluded recommendations for some treatments but not others.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Evaluating user experiences with an AI chatbot for health-related social needs: A cross-sectional mixed methods study

ai.headline: Caregivers found an AI chatbot easy to use and trustworthy for finding help with food, housing and money needs.
ai.summary: Researchers tested Daphne, an AI chatbot designed to identify unmet health-related social needs and suggest resources, with 128 caregivers of children with special healthcare needs. Nearly all participants reported unmet needs such as food insecurity or financial limitations, and they rated the chatbot highly for usability, satisfaction and trust, with sessions averaging about three minutes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a simple digital tool could help families get support for everyday problems like food, bills and transport between clinic visits.
ai.life_skill: Try using a trusted chatbot or helpline to find local support if you are struggling with food, housing, bills or transport.
ai.fact: Nearly all caregivers in the study reported at least one unmet health-related social need.

quiz.question: What did caregivers say about using the Daphne chatbot?
quiz.answer: They found it easy to use, satisfying and trustworthy, with short sessions averaging about three minutes.

ai.caveat: This was a single cross-sectional study, so it shows user experience at one point in time rather than proving the chatbot improves health over the long term.

items.title: Short-Lived Hyperglycaemia Contributes to Continuous Glucose Monitoring Metrics Used for Therapeutic Decision-Making

ai.headline: Brief blood sugar spikes can change diabetes monitoring readings even when overall results look similar.
ai.summary: Researchers looked at continuous glucose monitor data from 135 children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes. Short-lived hyperglycaemia—brief high blood sugar episodes lasting 10 to 60 minutes—was common and raised daytime average glucose while lowering time in range, especially around meals.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that two people with similar overall glucose readings may have very different patterns of brief spikes, which matters for understanding diabetes data and avoiding unnecessary treatment changes.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether high readings are brief and isolated before assuming overall control has worsened.
ai.fact: Short-lived hyperglycaemic episodes made up 18.5% of daytime hyperglycaemic episodes in the studied group.

quiz.question: What did removing short-lived hyperglycaemia do to daytime time in range?
quiz.answer: It increased daytime time in range by 1.74 percentage points.

ai.caveat: This is a single-centre retrospective preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary and may not apply more widely.

items.title: Exploring the Potential of Symbolic Regression in Precision Livestock Farming

ai.headline: An explainable AI method predicted when pigs will give birth within about nine hours on average.
ai.summary: Researchers used sensor data from sows to detect nest-building behaviour and predict the remaining time until farrowing. Symbolic regression, an open-box AI method, produced a mathematical formula and achieved a mean average error of 9.28 hours, outperforming closed-box models such as support vector regression and neural networks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how interpretable AI could help farmers protect piglet survival and sow welfare without relying on opaque black-box predictions.
ai.life_skill: Try choosing tools that explain how they reach a conclusion, not just tools that give an answer.
ai.fact: Symbolic regression generates interpretable mathematical formulas rather than closed-box predictions.

quiz.question: What was the average error of the symbolic regression model in predicting time to farrowing?
quiz.answer: The mean absolute error was 9.28 hours.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Brain representations of visual short-term memories during healthy human aging: occipital decline and frontoparietal compensation

ai.headline: Visual short-term memory fades with age, but other brain areas may partly compensate.
ai.summary: Researchers scanned 115 adults aged 25–87 while they remembered motion directions. Visual brain areas showed weaker memory signals with age, which explained part of the age-related drop in memory performance, while frontoparietal areas showed stronger signals with age during memory maintenance and partly offset the decline.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that age-related memory changes involve different brain systems, not just one simple decline.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you need to hold something in mind briefly and use reminders or repetition rather than relying on memory alone.
ai.fact: Visual short-term memory representations weaken with age in visual cortex, while frontoparietal representations can strengthen with age during memory maintenance.

quiz.question: Which brain region showed stronger memory-related signals with age during memory maintenance?
quiz.answer: Frontoparietal regions showed stronger representations with age during maintenance.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it is an observational study, so it cannot prove that frontoparietal activity causes the compensation.

items.title: Profiling phubbing practitioners using machine learning

ai.headline: Phubbing linked to personality traits
ai.summary: Researchers studied phubbing behaviors in Brazilian adults, analyzing personality traits and Instagram use. They identified five distinct profiles of phubbing practitioners. The profiles differed in problematic Instagram use and personality traits like Conscientiousness and Extraversion.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding phubbing behaviors can help individuals recognize their own digital habits and potential negative impacts on relationships
ai.life_skill: Notice how your phone use affects your interactions with others
ai.fact: Phubbing behaviors are linked to different personality traits and digital habits

quiz.question: What was used to analyze the indicators of phubbing behaviors?
quiz.answer: Gaussian Mixture Models with alternative covariance structures were used.

ai.caveat: The study's findings are based on a single sample of Brazilian adults and require longitudinal and independent replication to confirm their stability and practical relevance.

items.title: Young Canadians focus on mental health at key climate trial

ai.headline: Young climate plaintiffs in Canada are highlighting their mental health in a landmark trial against the government.

items.title: Alcohol use and its associations with mental health across the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic

ai.headline: Alcohol use stayed mostly stable during the first pandemic year, but loneliness predicted drinking more later.
ai.summary: Researchers tracked 2,369 people aged 11 to 100 across the UK, US and Australia for one year. Drinking frequency and quantity stayed stable overall, though young people aged 11-20 and mid-aged people aged 50-70 were most likely to increase how often and how much they drank. items.title: Beyond the Battlefield: A Cross-Sectional Study of War-Related Stressors and Mental Health in Four Central European Countries

ai.headline: War-related stress may affect mental health in countries not directly fighting, with coping styles linked to symptoms.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed nearly 3,000 adults in Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary more than two years after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Poland had the highest average scores for psychological distress, anxiety and depressive symptoms, while Czechia had the lowest for distress and anxiety. Greater use of emotion-focused coping was linked to higher symptom scores, and problem-focused coping was linked to lower scores only in Poland.

ai.headline: Pregnant women in Ghana see pre-eclampsia as serious but face cost, mistrust and poor communication when seeking care.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 16 pregnant women in Ghana’s Ashanti Region about their beliefs regarding pre-eclampsia. items.title: Empirical validation of a predicted emotional modulation dimension linking temporal variability and individual differences in PTSD

ai.headline: PTSD symptoms fluctuate along a specific balance between re-experiencing and avoidance, not just overall severity.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed data from nine PTSD cohorts to see if symptom changes over time follow the same patterns as differences between people. They found that both individual differences and daily fluctuations are organised by a 'symptom imbalance' axis, where two common therapies reduce severity but shift this balance in opposite directions.

items.title: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation

ai.headline: A new framework checks whether AI computer-use agents notice changes that happen while they work.
ai.summary: The paper introduces EnvOS, a way to test AI agents in software that changes mid-task, such as an appointment moving or a policy being revised. ai.summary: Researchers bred seed beetles for over 200 generations to create short- and long-lived lines, nearly doubling lifespan. ai.why_it_matters: It shows that lifespan is influenced by many genetic factors working together and can differ between males and females, helping scientists understand the biology of ageing.
ai.fact: Lifespan evolution in beetles involved many genes and structural DNA changes, with some effects differing between the sexes.
