quiz.question: What was the strongest predictor of favourable views of AI across all countries studied?
quiz.answer: General optimism about science and technology.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the data are provisional, so the findings should be treated as preliminary rather than confirmed.

items.title: Pallidal Local Field Potentials markers of dystonia aetiology and severity in children

ai.headline: Brain-wave patterns in a movement-control area are linked to how severe childhood dystonia is.
ai.summary: Researchers recorded electrical activity from the globus pallidus internus in 30 children and young adults with severe dystonia before deep brain stimulation. Delta and low-gamma peak power, plus coordination between the two sides of the brain, were linked to symptom severity, while low-gamma power differed between genetic and acquired dystonia.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how brain signals might one day help track or understand a childhood movement disorder across different causes.
ai.fact: Delta and low-gamma peak power in the globus pallidus internus were significantly linked to dystonia severity in children, regardless of medication, brain structure, or cause.

quiz.question: Which brain-wave peak powers were significantly linked to dystonia severity in children?
quiz.answer: Delta and low-gamma peak power were significantly linked to dystonia severity.

ai.caveat: This is a small, preprint observational study that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary and not proof.

items.title: Sentiment Analysis of Thought-Related Language in the Context of Cognitive Disorders Using Machine Learning, Transformer-based Architecture and Large Language Models

ai.headline: Machine learning analyzes thought patterns
ai.summary: Researchers studied sentiment analysis of thought-related language using machine learning models. They found that lightweight models and distilled transformers were effective for large-scale sentiment analysis. The study used a large dataset of social media texts to evaluate the performance of various models.
ai.why_it_matters: This research could lead to innovative methods for addressing negative thought patterns and improving mental health
ai.life_skill: Try to be aware of your thoughts and emotions to better understand your mental well-being
ai.fact: Machine learning models can be used to analyze sentiment polarity in thought-related text

quiz.question: What type of texts were used to evaluate the performance of the models?
quiz.answer: Social media texts

ai.caveat: The study is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution

items.title: Structural limits of single-barrier reform in algorithmic recourse: A formal series-system model with implications for digital health

ai.headline: Fixing just one barrier in algorithmic recourse is unlikely to help much; coordinated reform may be needed.
ai.summary: The paper models getting recourse after an adverse algorithmic decision as 11 barriers across three layers: data integration, data accuracy, and institutional access. Under its baseline calibration, the chance of clearing all barriers is 0.0018%, and removing any single barrier improves this by less than 0.02%. The model suggests that most achievable improvement comes from coordinated action across all three layers rather than isolated fixes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why appealing an automated decision can feel nearly impossible and why piecemeal reforms may fail without broader, joined-up changes.
ai.life_skill: If you are challenging an automated decision, check whether several linked barriers need fixing at once rather than focusing on just one.
ai.fact: The model estimates end-to-end recourse probability at 0.0018% under its baseline parameters.

quiz.question: What does the model say about fixing only one barrier to algorithmic recourse?
quiz.answer: Removing any single barrier yields negligible improvement, below 0.02%, because the barriers compound multiplicatively.

ai.caveat: The findings are properties of a mathematical model, not measurements of real-world recourse pathways, and await validation against observed data.

items.title: REAL Parenting Alcohol and Substance Use App

ai.headline: A trial is testing whether a digital app helps parents talk to teens about alcohol, nicotine and marijuana.
ai.summary: Researchers are running a randomised trial of REAL Parenting, a digital version of a parent handbook covering alcohol, nicotine and marijuana use. Parent-teen dyads will be split so some parents receive the app materials and others receive active control materials. The study will examine whether the app affects teen alcohol use and related consequences over time.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how researchers are trying to give parents practical, on-the-go tools to discuss substance use with their teenage children.
ai.fact: The study is a randomised controlled trial, meaning families are assigned by chance to different groups so the app’s effects can be compared fairly.

quiz.question: What is the REAL Parenting trial testing?
quiz.answer: Whether a digital app for parents affects teenagers’ alcohol, nicotine and marijuana use and related consequences.

ai.caveat: The abstract describes a planned trial and reports no results, so it cannot show whether the app actually works.

items.title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds

ai.headline: AI models can teach themselves physical reasoning by building simulated worlds and testing outcomes without human-made data.
ai.summary: The study tested a self-evolving AI framework where a vision-language model proposes executable physical worlds, and a physics engine simulates baseline and counterfactual outcomes to create training tasks. The model improved on physical reasoning benchmarks, especially on questions involving changed worlds and interactions with cloth, fluids, and soft bodies.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI might learn cause-and-effect in the physical world by simulating alternatives, which could help robots and other embodied systems act more reliably in everyday environments.
ai.life_skill: Try imagining how a situation would change if one object or action were removed before deciding what to do.
ai.fact: The framework improved scores on physical reasoning benchmarks without using human-labelled intervention data.

quiz.question: What did the physics engine do in this framework?
quiz.answer: It simulated matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches to create answer-bound visual tasks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and the findings come from AI benchmark tests rather than real-world human behaviour.

items.title: Acute social defeat induces cannabinoid type 1 receptor-dependent synaptic depression in the anterior ventral subiculum to anterior hypothalamic nucleus pathway to drive social avoidance in male mice

ai.headline: A specific brain pathway in male mice controls stress-induced social avoidance through cannabinoid receptors.
ai.summary: Researchers studied male mice exposed to acute social defeat stress and found that activity in a pathway from the front part of the ventral subiculum to the anterior hypothalamic nucleus was suppressed via glucocorticoid and cannabinoid type 1 receptor mechanisms, leading to social avoidance. Activating this pathway increased social approach, while inhibiting it caused avoidance even after mild stress.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how stress can make social withdrawal happen at the level of specific brain circuits.
ai.life_skill: Notice when stress makes you want to avoid people and consider reaching out anyway.
ai.fact: In male mice, the anterior ventral subiculum to anterior hypothalamic nucleus pathway is linked to social avoidance after acute social defeat stress.

quiz.question: What happened when researchers activated the avSUB to AHN pathway in stressed male mice?
quiz.answer: It produced an immediate increase in social approach.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint in male mice, not yet peer reviewed, so the findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: When Cash Wakes Up: Inertia in Institutional Money Market Funds and the Potential Effects of AI Disruption -- by Ali Hortaçsu, Younggeun Yoo

ai.headline: Institutional cash management is inertial
ai.summary: Researchers studied institutional cash management by analyzing money market funds held by mutual funds from 2010 to 2024. They found high inertia, with over half of mutual funds never switching their money market fund choice despite yield differences. The study also explored the potential effects of AI disruption on this inertia.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because understanding cash management inertia can help investors and financial institutions make more informed decisions
ai.life_skill: Check the yields of your money market funds regularly
ai.fact: Many institutional investors exhibit high inertia in their cash management decisions

quiz.question: What happens to fees if AI-driven automation reduces investor inattention?
quiz.answer: Fees fall by approximately half

ai.caveat: This is a preprint study and its findings have not been peer reviewed, so the results should be interpreted with caution

items.title: The asteroid that killed the dinosaurs may have helped ants conquer the world

ai.headline: An asteroid strike may have helped ants spread worldwide by boosting their sense of smell through jumping genes.
ai.summary: Researchers studied the link between the dinosaur-killing asteroid and the rise of major ant groups. They found that bursts of activity from mobile genetic elements called jumping genes coincided with this rise and may have sharpened ants’ ability to communicate through smell.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a single ancient event can shape which living things dominate the planet today.
ai.life_skill: Notice how ants use scent trails to find food and work together.
ai.fact: Ants communicate largely through smell.

quiz.question: What may have helped sharpen ants’ ability to communicate through smell?
quiz.answer: Bursts of activity from mobile genetic elements called jumping genes coincided with the rise of major ant groups.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a study, not the full research, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Clinical Evidence of Orally Administered Herbal Preparations for Supportive Cancer Care: A PRISMA Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials (1990-2026).

ai.headline: A review of eight trials found no reliable evidence that oral herbal preparations help or are safe for people with cancer.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed eight randomised trials of oral herbal preparations in people with cancer. Some small studies hinted at benefits for sleep, fatigue, appetite, anxiety, mouth dryness, stomach symptoms and quality of life, but one trial found no benefit for fatigue or quality of life, and all evidence was rated very low certainty.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that popular herbal products for cancer symptoms are not yet proven to work or to be safe, so people should not rely on them instead of standard care.
ai.life_skill: Talk to your oncology team before taking any herbal preparation during cancer treatment.
ai.fact: No serious herb-related adverse events were reported across the eight trials, but safety monitoring was inconsistent and no trial was large enough to establish safety.

quiz.question: What did the review conclude about using oral herbal preparations routinely in cancer care?
quiz.answer: The evidence is insufficient to establish efficacy or safety or to support routine clinical implementation.

ai.caveat: The review included only eight small, very different trials with high risk of bias and very low certainty evidence, so no firm conclusions can be drawn.

items.title: Music-based interventions for people with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Music may reduce short-term fatigue for people on haemodialysis, but most evidence is very uncertain.
ai.summary: This Cochrane systematic review looked at 27 randomised trials involving 1,584 people with kidney failure receiving haemodialysis. It found music-based interventions may reduce short-term fatigue compared with usual care or other comparators, but evidence for blood pressure and most other outcomes was very uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a low-cost, non-drug option that might help with a common symptom, while highlighting that stronger evidence is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Try listening to music during haemodialysis sessions if you find it relaxing, but discuss any symptom changes with your dialysis team.
ai.fact: The review included 27 studies from 13 countries and territories across Asia, Europe, North America, and South America.

quiz.question: What did the review find about short-term fatigue?
quiz.answer: Music-based interventions may reduce short-term fatigue compared with usual care or other comparators, based on low-certainty evidence from one study.

ai.caveat: Most findings were based on very low-certainty evidence, so the true effects could be substantially different.

items.title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on metabolic syndrome parameters in adults: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials exploring the role of baseline vitamin D status and supplementation dose

ai.headline: Vitamin D supplements may slightly improve some metabolic syndrome markers, especially in people who are deficient.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at eight randomised trials involving 634 adults with metabolic syndrome who took oral vitamin D for at least eight weeks. Supplements reliably raised blood vitamin D levels, and some trials reported improvements in triglycerides, insulin resistance, waist circumference and BMI, though blood pressure, HDL cholesterol and fasting glucose did not consistently change. Benefits appeared strongest in people who started with low vitamin D and used higher doses, but the evidence is uncertain because most trials had some or high risk of bias and none was designed to test these subgroup patterns formally.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that correcting vitamin D deficiency might offer modest metabolic benefits, but it is not yet proven enough to rely on for managing metabolic syndrome.
ai.life_skill: If you have metabolic syndrome, ask a qualified health professional whether checking and treating a possible vitamin D deficiency is appropriate for you.
ai.fact: Metabolic syndrome is a cluster of conditions including central obesity, high blood sugar, high blood pressure and abnormal blood fats.

quiz.question: Which metabolic measures showed no consistent change across most trials in the review?
quiz.answer: Blood pressure, HDL-cholesterol and fasting glucose showed no consistent change across the majority of trials.

ai.caveat: The review is based on only eight small trials, most with some or high risk of bias, and the subgroup patterns by baseline vitamin D status and dose were exploratory rather than formally tested.

items.title: The effects of physical exercise on executive function, internalizing symptoms and externalizing symptoms in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Physical exercise may improve inhibitory control in children and adolescents with ADHD, but evidence is weak.
ai.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 25 randomised controlled trials with 1,116 participants looked at physical exercise in children and adolescents with ADHD. It found a statistically significant effect on inhibitory control, but no clear effects on cognitive flexibility, working memory, internalizing symptoms, or externalizing symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests exercise could be a helpful addition to support for young people with ADHD, but the evidence is not strong enough to rely on alone.
ai.life_skill: Try regular physical activity as one part of managing ADHD, alongside professional support.
ai.fact: The review included 25 randomised controlled trials involving 1,116 participants.

quiz.question: Which outcome showed a statistically significant improvement with physical exercise?
quiz.answer: Inhibitory control showed a statistically significant effect, while the other outcomes did not.

ai.caveat: The evidence was rated low or very low certainty, with high heterogeneity, wide confidence intervals, and limited stability.

items.title: Outdoor risky play and health-related outcomes in children aged 3–12 years: A mixed-methods systematic review

ai.headline: Outdoor risky play is linked to better health and development in children aged 3–12, but evidence quality is low-to-moderate.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 74 studies looked at outdoor risky play in children aged 3–12 and its links to health outcomes. General risky play and environments that support it were positively associated with physical, mental, social, cognitive and risk-competence outcomes; independent mobility was linked to more physical activity, while rough-and-tumble play showed mixed results except for a link to increased aggression.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests everyday outdoor play that feels a bit risky may support children’s health and development, though stronger evidence is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Try letting children explore outdoor play that feels slightly risky, such as climbing or balancing, within safe limits.
ai.fact: Outdoor risky play is positively associated with several health and development domains in children aged 3–12.

quiz.question: What did the review find about independent mobility?
quiz.answer: It was positively associated with physical activity, with insufficient evidence for other health domains.

ai.caveat: The overall quality of evidence was low-to-moderate, so the findings are promising but not yet firm proof.

items.title: Cumulative Prenatal Adversity and Fronto-Limbic White Matter Development Across Adolescence

ai.headline: More prenatal adversity is linked to lower brain white-matter quality at the start of adolescence.
ai.summary: Researchers studied over 10,000 US children aged about 10 to 16 and found that a higher count of adverse prenatal exposures was linked to lower fractional anisotropy in several fronto-limbic white-matter tracts at baseline. The same burden was also linked to involuntary emotional dysregulation, partly through these white-matter differences.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests early-life conditions before birth may be biologically linked to how the brain develops and how teenagers manage emotions.
ai.life_skill: Notice if strong emotions feel hard to control and consider speaking with a trusted adult or counsellor.
ai.fact: Higher cumulative prenatal adversity was associated with lower baseline fractional anisotropy in the left uncinate fasciculus, corpus callosum and right uncinate fasciculus.

quiz.question: What was higher prenatal adversity linked to at the start of adolescence?
quiz.answer: Lower fractional anisotropy in several fronto-limbic white-matter tracts.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot show that prenatal adversity caused the brain differences.

items.title: Psychological preparation in multimodal cancer prehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-synthesis of patients’ experiences

ai.headline: Psychological preparation in cancer prehabilitation comes from the whole programme, not just psychological support.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 17 reports on adults’ experiences of multimodal cancer prehabilitation across six high-income countries. Patients found psychological preparation through exercise, dietary support, and relationships with staff and peers, rather than through explicitly psychological input alone.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that useful psychological preparation can arise from everyday parts of a treatment programme and from feeling supported, not only from formal therapy.
ai.life_skill: Notice which parts of a programme or routine actually help you feel more prepared, rather than assuming only the obviously ‘psychological’ bits count.
ai.fact: Patients described psychological preparation as having something to act on, discovering what their bodies could do, understanding what was coming, being taken seriously, and not being alone.

quiz.question: According to the review, where did patients say psychological preparation mainly come from?
quiz.answer: It arose from exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only from explicitly psychological input.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and the evidence came almost entirely from people who engaged with prehabilitation, with staff training, adherence and fidelity sparsely reported.

items.title: Beyond Sleep Duration: Sleep Regularity, Emotional Memory, and Prefrontal–Limbic Development in Adolescence
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

ai.headline: Sleep regularity may matter for emotional memory and brain development in teenagers, but more research is needed.
ai.summary: This narrative review looked at how sleep regularity, emotional memory, and adolescent brain development are connected. It discusses the amygdala, hippocampus, and prefrontal cortex and highlights gaps in evidence about how sleep regularity independently affects emotional memory in teenagers.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that sleep patterns beyond just how long you sleep could influence how teenagers process emotions and memories.
ai.life_skill: Try going to bed and waking up at similar times each day.
ai.fact: Sleep regularity is distinct from sleep duration and timing.

quiz.question: What does the review say about the evidence linking sleep regularity to emotional memory in adolescents?
quiz.answer: There are gaps in evidence regarding their independent associations.

ai.caveat: It is a narrative review proposing future research, not new experimental findings.

items.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care

ai.headline: AI models good at diagnosing cancer may fail at later stages of care, a new benchmark shows.
ai.summary: Researchers created a benchmark using records from 405 patients across six cancer-care phases to test 30 AI models. Models that performed well at diagnosis did not reliably perform well in later care, and their main errors changed depending on the care phase.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools trusted for one medical task cannot be assumed to stay safe or accurate throughout a patient’s long-term treatment.
ai.life_skill: Check whether any AI health tool you use is designed for the specific stage of care you need, not just diagnosis.
ai.fact: In this study, explicit decision errors were most common in anatomical staging, while decision omissions were most common in initial work-up and post-treatment follow-up.

quiz.question: Did high diagnostic performance translate into improved downstream cancer care in the evaluated AI models?
quiz.answer: No, high diagnostic performance did not translate into improved downstream care.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and it evaluates AI models using simulated patient records rather than real patient outcomes.

items.title: Rethinking Consciousness: The Self-Organising Information-Processing Systems Hypothesis

ai.headline: A new theory proposes consciousness emerges from self-organising information systems across biology, AI and social groups.
ai.summary: The paper introduces the Self-Organising Information-Processing Systems (SOIPS) Hypothesis. It suggests that interacting parts can organise themselves into structures that support functions such as perception, memory, learning and consciousness, without those functions being specified in advance. Consciousness is described as awareness-related information taking part in flexible cognition, not something limited to humans or an inevitable result of complexity.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a shared way to think about how minds, artificial intelligence and group behaviour might develop complex capabilities from simpler parts.
ai.life_skill: Notice how information you pay attention to shapes the choices you make next.
ai.fact: Consciousness is proposed as a configuration where awareness-related information participates in flexible cognition, rather than being restricted to human biology.

quiz.question: According to SOIPS, is consciousness limited to human biology?
quiz.answer: No, consciousness is not restricted by definition to human biology.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint theory paper, not peer-reviewed evidence, so its claims are speculative and untested.

items.title: Exercise From Afar: Progressing At Risk Individuals to Independent Exercise

ai.headline: A remote app-based exercise program is being tested to improve fitness and dementia-risk markers in underactive rural adults.
ai.summary: The study recruits 50 underactive adults aged 40–70 from rural Kansas counties. They use a fitness app to follow personalised exercise sessions at home, record technique videos for feedback, and repeat fitness and health assessments after the program to measure changes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how technology might help people in remote areas exercise independently and potentially lower factors linked to dementia risk.
ai.life_skill: Try using a reputable fitness app with video guidance to build a regular home exercise habit.
ai.fact: Physical inactivity is linked to higher risk of cognitive decline and dementia.

quiz.question: Who is being recruited for the exercise study?
quiz.answer: Underactive adults aged 40–70 from federally designated rural and frontier Kansas counties.

ai.caveat: This is a trial registration with posted results information, not a full peer-reviewed publication, so the findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents

ai.headline: Writing down your claims and confidence before hearing criticism helps you avoid wrongly changing your mind.
ai.summary: The study tested an AI method called Thinking-in-Bets, where an agent records its main claims, supporting checks, and confidence before reading user feedback. Agents that did this were far less likely to abandon correct work when wrongly challenged, while still being able to fix real mistakes. Writing the record after hearing the complaint gave almost no benefit.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that pausing to note what you believe and why before hearing pushback can help you hold your ground when you are right, while still staying open to genuine correction.
ai.life_skill: Before reacting to criticism, jot down your main points, the evidence for each, and how sure you are.
ai.fact: Recording key claims and confidence before receiving feedback reduces false reversals in AI agents across software engineering, report writing, finance, and command-line tasks.

quiz.question: When did recording claims before feedback help AI agents most?
quiz.answer: It helped when the record was written before reading the complaint, not after.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and tested only on specific AI models and benchmarks, so the results may not generalise to people or other systems.

items.title: Training Your Replacement: Worker Incentives and the Pace of Automation -- by Joshua S. Gans, Peter Landry

ai.headline: Workers may be paid more to train AI that replaces them, but firms can slow training without a bonus.
ai.summary: The paper models a situation where workers can cooperate with, shirk, or obstruct training AI systems that will replace them. Because dismissal is a weaker threat once training ends the job, firms must pay workers extra rent, and workers can gain from their own replacement. A completion bonus equal to that rent removes both the worker’s gain and any slowdown in training.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how AI adoption can change wages and job security even before a job is automated.
ai.life_skill: Notice when training a new tool could change your role, and ask how your pay or job security is protected.
ai.fact: AI can create jobs paying more than they produce and eliminate jobs it never automates.

quiz.question: What happens to the threat of dismissal once AI training ends the worker’s job?
quiz.answer: Dismissal becomes a weaker penalty for shirking.

ai.caveat: This is a theoretical model in a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so it does not show what happens in real workplaces.

items.title: Students' love-hate relationship with AI

ai.headline: Generative AI spread quickly among engineering students at EPFL after ChatGPT launched.
ai.summary: The piece describes how ChatGPT rapidly reached students' computers and smartphones at EPFL within two years, helped by students' adaptable learning habits and the growing number of AI models.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how quickly new digital tools can become part of everyday student life and learning.
ai.life_skill: Notice how often you rely on AI for study tasks and check whether you still understand the work yourself.
ai.fact: Generative AI spread rapidly among EPFL students within two years of ChatGPT's launch.

quiz.question: What helped generative AI spread quickly among EPFL students?
quiz.answer: Students' still-malleable learning habits and the growing number of AI models and improvements to them.

ai.caveat: This is a short news report, not a research study, so it does not provide evidence of effects or outcomes.

items.title: Sensitivity of stochastic growth rate and lifetime reproductive output to kin effects: A nonlinear feedback model

ai.headline: Close kin presence is linked to lower child mortality and may shape how social behaviour evolves.
ai.summary: The study models how kinship networks and life history influence each other, focusing on mothers, grandmothers, and older sisters. It finds that kin presence is negatively linked to child mortality, and that strengthening these kin effects is linked to higher population growth and lifetime reproductive output.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how family support can be linked to child survival and the evolution of social behaviour across generations.
ai.life_skill: Notice how close relatives support children in your family or community.
ai.fact: The presence of mothers, grandmothers, and older sisters is linked to lower child mortality in the studied populations.

quiz.question: What was the study's main finding about close kin and child mortality?
quiz.answer: The presence of mothers, grandmothers, and older sisters was negatively linked to child mortality, meaning it was associated with lower mortality.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and relies on a theoretical model rather than direct experimental proof.

items.title: AI governance needs to consider users’ emotional responses

ai.headline: People often trust AI based on feelings rather than reliability, so governance should address emotional design.
ai.summary: The paper discusses how people often trust or distrust AI outputs because of how they make them feel rather than how reliable they are. It argues that AI governance frameworks should require platforms to disclose design choices that target user emotions, give users control over these, and include features to calibrate trust.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because emotional reactions to AI can shape everyday decisions, even when the AI is not actually reliable.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your trust in an AI tool comes from how it makes you feel or from evidence that it is reliable.
ai.fact: People often trust or distrust AI outputs based on how they feel rather than how reliable they are.

quiz.question: Why might someone trust or distrust an AI output according to the paper?
quiz.answer: Because of how it makes them feel rather than how reliable it is.

ai.caveat: This is a commentary article rather than a study with new data, so it presents arguments rather than proven findings.

items.title: The transcription factor BCL11A restores differentiation potential to aged oligodendrocyte progenitor cells

ai.headline: A specific protein helps restore the ability of aged brain cells to repair nerve insulation.
ai.summary: Researchers found that a protein called BCL11A, which naturally declines with age, is crucial for brain cells to mature and repair damaged nerves. In mice, boosting this protein helped aged cells repair spinal cord injuries more effectively.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how the brain loses its repair capacity with age could lead to future treatments for conditions like multiple sclerosis or age-related cognitive decline.
ai.fact: The BCL11A protein has remained largely unchanged throughout vertebrate evolution, suggesting it plays a critical role in brain development and maintenance.

quiz.question: What happened when researchers increased BCL11A levels in aged mouse cells?
quiz.answer: The aged cells showed significantly enhanced differentiation into myelinating oligodendrocytes without affecting their proliferation.

ai.caveat: These results were obtained in mice and cell models, so it is not yet proven that this approach will work safely or effectively in humans.

items.title: Perceived Classroom Goal Structures, Growth Mindset, Self-Regulated Learning, and Mathematics Performance among Chinese Middle School Students

ai.headline: Classrooms focused on mastery help students develop growth mindsets and better math skills.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 926 Chinese middle school students to see how classroom goals affect learning. They found that when students perceive a focus on mastery, they are more likely to have a growth mindset and use self-regulated learning strategies, which is linked to higher math performance.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding that the classroom environment shapes how you approach challenges can help you recognise when you are in a supportive learning space.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your current environment rewards effort and improvement or just final results.
ai.fact: Perceived mastery goal structures in classrooms are positively associated with students' growth mindset and self-regulated learning strategies.

quiz.question: What type of classroom goal structure was linked to better math performance?
quiz.answer: Perceived mastery goal structures were positively linked to growth mindset and self-regulated learning, which were linked to higher performance.

ai.caveat: This is a correlational study, so it cannot prove that changing classroom goals directly causes better math scores.

items.title: Exercise doesn't just strengthen your heart. It rewires it

ai.headline: Exercise reshapes the nerves controlling the heart, differently on the left and right sides.
ai.summary: Researchers studied how regular exercise affects the heart. They found it changes the nerves that control heart function, and these changes differ between the left and right sides of the body.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that exercise affects the heart’s wiring in more specific ways than previously thought.
ai.life_skill: Try regular physical activity as part of everyday life.
ai.fact: Exercise can reshape the nerves that control how the heart works, with different effects on the left and right sides.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about exercise and the nerves controlling the heart?
quiz.answer: It reshapes those nerves, and the changes differ between the left and right sides of the body.

ai.caveat: This is a news summary rather than the full research paper, so the study’s methods and reliability are not clear.

items.title: Large meta-analysis sheds new light on how SGLT2 inhibitors affect blood and iron parameters

ai.headline: SGLT2 inhibitors for diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease consistently raise blood haemoglobin and haematocrit levels.
ai.summary: Researchers studied SGLT2 inhibitors, drugs used to treat type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease. A large meta-analysis found these medicines consistently increase haemoglobin and haematocrit levels. The work was led by Dr Michele Eisenga.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people understand how a common class of medicines can change routine blood test results.
ai.fact: SGLT2 inhibitors consistently increase haemoglobin and haematocrit levels in people treated for type 2 diabetes, heart failure or chronic kidney disease.

quiz.question: What effect do SGLT2 inhibitors have on haemoglobin and haematocrit?
quiz.answer: They consistently increase both haemoglobin and haematocrit levels.

ai.caveat: This is based on a news report and abstract only, so the full study details and effect size are not available.

items.title: Predatory amphibians swam the seas 237 million years ago

ai.headline: A 237-million-year-old fossil from China suggests amphibians once lived in the sea.

items.title: Light-entrained chromatin priming poises rapid metamorphosis in a marine sponge

quiz.answer: They used variation in DNA sharing between 500,000 sibling pairs.

items.title: Intravenous iron supplementation in heart failure and iron deficiency: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

ai.headline: Intravenous iron may reduce heart failure hospitalisation, but evidence on mortality and function remains uncertain.
ai.summary: This umbrella review examined 18 systematic reviews of intravenous iron in people with heart failure and iron deficiency. It found the most consistent link was with fewer heart failure hospitalisations, while effects on death, fitness and quality of life were uncertain due to low-quality reviews and overlapping trials.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a common treatment for iron deficiency in heart failure may help keep people out of hospital, but the evidence is not yet strong enough to be certain.
ai.life_skill: If you have heart failure, discuss iron status and treatment options with your cardiologist or GP rather than assuming supplements will help.
ai.fact: Iron deficiency is common in heart failure and is linked to exercise intolerance, poorer health and repeated hospitalisation.

quiz.question: What outcome did the reviews most consistently link to intravenous iron in heart failure?
quiz.answer: Reduced heart failure hospitalisation, including recurrent hospitalisation and combined hospitalisation-cardiovascular death endpoints.

ai.caveat: The underlying reviews had low methodological quality, trials were substantially overlapping, and certainty of evidence was low or very low for most outcomes.

items.title: Psychological preparation in multimodal cancer prehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-synthesis of patients’ experiences

ai.headline: Psychological preparation in cancer prehabilitation comes from the whole programme, not just psychological support.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-synthesis looked at 17 qualitative studies involving 230 adults who took part in multimodal cancer prehabilitation combining exercise, nutrition and psychological support. Patients experienced psychological preparation as having something to act on, discovering what their bodies could do, understanding what was coming, being taken seriously, and not being alone. These benefits arose through exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only explicitly psychological input.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how cancer prehabilitation is delivered and matched to patients can shape their ability to cope before treatment.
ai.life_skill: Notice which parts of a support programme feel most useful to you and tell your care team so they can match help to what you can use.
ai.fact: Psychological preparation in cancer prehabilitation can arise from exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only explicitly psychological input.

quiz.question: According to the review, where did patients say psychological preparation came from?
quiz.answer: It arose through exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only explicitly psychological input.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and evidence came almost entirely from people who engaged with prehabilitation, with staff training, adherence and fidelity sparsely reported.

items.title: Adolescents' mental health, well-being, and biopsychological stress in school: a narrative review of school-related correlates and interventions

ai.headline: Schools can support adolescent mental health through relationships, skills, and targeted interventions, though results vary.
ai.summary: This narrative review examined research on adolescents' mental health, well-being, and stress in school settings. It found that supportive teacher and peer relationships, along with individual skills like coping and motivation, are linked to positive development, while school-based interventions such as social and emotional learning and mindfulness show mixed effectiveness.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that academic progress and student well-being can support each other rather than compete.
ai.life_skill: Notice which school relationships and habits help you feel calmer and more capable.
ai.fact: Mental health is more than the absence of mental illness; it includes positive well-being and functioning.

quiz.question: What does the review say about the effectiveness of school-based mental health interventions?
quiz.answer: Findings remain heterogeneous, particularly regarding intervention effectiveness.

ai.caveat: A narrative review summarises existing studies rather than providing new, pooled evidence, and the authors note that findings are mixed and more rigorous research is needed.

items.title: Depression in Women on a Global Level: Cultural Perspectives, Social Determinants, Gender Inequalities, and Implications for Mental Health Care
items.venue: British journal of healthcare and medical research

ai.headline: Women worldwide have higher rates of depression than men, shaped by social and cultural factors.
ai.summary: This review examined research on depression among women globally. It found women consistently experience higher rates than men, linked to poverty, violence, caregiving, reproductive health, and barriers to care, with cultural beliefs affecting how symptoms are expressed and treated.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how social conditions and culture influence mental health, helping people recognise that depression is not just an individual problem.
ai.life_skill: Notice how stress, relationships, and life changes affect your mood, and consider speaking to a trusted person or professional if low mood persists.
ai.fact: Depression is a leading cause of disability worldwide.

quiz.question: Do women consistently experience higher rates of depression than men across diverse contexts?
quiz.answer: Yes, the review found women consistently experience higher rates of depression than men across diverse cultural, social, and economic contexts.

ai.caveat: This is an integrative review synthesising existing literature rather than new primary evidence, so findings depend on the quality of the studies included.

items.title: Community burden of diphtheria during the 2023-24 epidemic in Kano State, Nigeria: a population-based household survey

ai.headline: A household survey found diphtheria was more common in Kano communities than official clinic records showed.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed nearly 8,000 people in four Nigerian local government areas during the 2023-24 diphtheria epidemic. They estimated a community attack rate of 1.1%, about three times the rate notified at three treatment sites, and found most deaths happened at home.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that clinic records can miss a large share of illness in the community, so outbreaks may be bigger than official figures suggest.
ai.life_skill: Check that your routine vaccinations are up to date and seek care quickly if you develop a serious sore throat or breathing difficulty.
ai.fact: Diphtheria is a serious infectious disease that can cause severe throat swelling and breathing problems.

quiz.question: How did the community attack rate compare with the rate notified at treatment sites?
quiz.answer: The community attack rate was about three times higher than the rate notified at three treatment sites.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and diphtheria, deaths and vaccination status were reported by respondents without laboratory or record confirmation.

items.title: College Success: Understanding the Roles of Financial Aid, Loans, Preparation, and Incentives -- by Douglas N. Harris, Christopher R. Taber, Alan Yang

ai.headline: Better college preparation may raise attainment more than financial aid alone.
ai.summary: The study models how financial aid, loans, incentives and pre-college skills affect college attendance and graduation. It finds most financial policies have moderate effects on attendance but small effects on completion, while better preparing students for college offers the greatest potential to increase attainment.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that money alone may not be enough to help more students finish college, and that skills before starting matter greatly.
ai.life_skill: Focus on building study and academic skills before starting college rather than relying only on financial support.
ai.fact: The earnings gap between college graduates and non-graduates has widened substantially over the past four decades.

quiz.question: What does the study find has the greatest potential for increasing college attainment?
quiz.answer: Better preparing students for college.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint using a simulation model rather than direct experimental proof, so the findings are not yet peer-reviewed or definitive.

items.title: Delayed Retirement, Intergenerational Transfers, and Fertility

ai.headline: Delaying retirement may cut grandparental childcare and lower fertility, especially for lower-income women.
ai.summary: The study models China’s gradual delayed-retirement reform and its effects on older adults’ work, money transfers to adult children, and grandparental childcare. Simulations suggest that while delayed retirement raises older employment and monetary transfers, it reduces childcare enough to lower fertility and older adults’ welfare, with larger losses among lower-income women. Childcare subsidies could offset these declines.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that retirement policy can affect family life and fertility through grandparental childcare, not just older adults’ work and income.
ai.life_skill: Notice how changes in grandparents’ work might affect the childcare they can provide to families.
ai.fact: Delayed retirement can reduce grandparental childcare even as it increases monetary transfers to adult children.

quiz.question: What happens to fertility when delayed retirement reduces grandparental childcare more than it increases monetary transfers?
quiz.answer: Fertility declines.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and relies on a model and simulations rather than direct observation of the reform’s outcomes.

items.title: Rethinking Consciousness: The Self-Organising Information-Processing Systems Hypothesis

ai.headline: A new theory suggests consciousness emerges from how information is organised and shared within systems, not just from biology.
ai.summary: The paper proposes the Self-Organising Information-Processing Systems Hypothesis. It suggests that when components interact and share information flexibly, they can develop capabilities like perception, memory and agency, and that consciousness may arise when awareness-related information supports flexible cognition.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a way to think about consciousness that could apply to brains, artificial intelligence and group behaviour rather than treating it as unique to humans.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different groups or systems you are part of share information to make decisions together.
ai.fact: Consciousness is proposed as a configuration in which awareness-related information participates in flexible cognition.

quiz.question: According to the SOIPS hypothesis, is consciousness limited to human biology?
quiz.answer: No, consciousness is not restricted by definition to human biology.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and a theoretical proposal, not peer-reviewed evidence or experimental proof.

items.title: Pedagogical resilience reconstruction in the AI era: a longitudinal reflexive thematic analysis of teacher reflective journals

ai.headline: Keeping an AI course running does not automatically mean students are learning.
ai.summary: The study followed one teacher's reflective journals over a 12-week AI course for first-year art students. The teacher found that students often mistook seeing, bookmarking, or one-click generation for actual ability, especially when teaching became demonstration-only and the final assessment did not require attendance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that high engagement with AI tools can hide a lack of real learning, which matters for anyone studying independently.
ai.life_skill: Check whether you can actually do the task yourself without watching a demo or using a one-click tool.
ai.fact: Students can appear highly engaged with AI tools while gaining little actual learning.

quiz.question: What did the teacher call the pattern where students treated seeing or one-click generation as being able to do?
quiz.answer: The teacher termed it a teacher-perceived low-threshold illusion.

ai.caveat: This is a single teacher's self-study based on their own journals, so the findings are not proof and cannot be generalised to all students or courses.

items.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders

ai.headline: A new method helps AI link map locations with satellite images and other data more effectively.
ai.summary: The study examined location encoders, which turn geographic coordinates into digital descriptions using satellite imagery. It found these tools are mathematically limited to two dimensions, but a new two-stage method called LoCA overcomes this by creating a shared, high-quality target from satellite data and training location and metadata encoders to match it.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because better location encoding can improve how we monitor land cover, wildfires, biodiversity and climate from space.
ai.life_skill: Try checking how satellite maps are used to track environmental changes in your area.
ai.fact: Location encoders convert geographic coordinates into high-dimensional digital descriptors using Earth observation imagery.

quiz.question: What did the researchers prove about standard location encoders?
quiz.answer: They proved that any Lipschitz location encoder produces an output of intrinsic dimension at most 2.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet established.

items.title: Comparing Embedded and End-of-Session Formative Quizzes: Implications for Engagement and Self-Regulated Learning in Psychology Classrooms

ai.headline: Short quizzes spread through a lecture boosted engagement and self-regulated learning more than quizzes at the end.
ai.summary: Researchers compared embedded quizzes during psychology lectures with the same quizzes given at the end of lectures among 81 third-year students. Students who took quizzes during the lecture reported higher cognitive engagement, situational interest, and self-regulated learning than those who quizzed at the end.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that when you quiz yourself during study can affect how interested and engaged you stay, not just what you learn.
ai.life_skill: Try breaking your revision into short self-quizzes spaced throughout a study session instead of saving them all for the end.
ai.fact: Quiz timing within a lesson is linked to students’ engagement and self-regulated learning.
ai.caveat: This was a small, non-randomised classroom study, so the results are not proof that quiz timing caused the differences.

items.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain

ai.headline: Older adults who closely follow a Mediterranean diet may have higher levels of two heart- and brain-protecting proteins.
ai.summary: Researchers studied older adults and found that those who closely followed a Mediterranean diet had higher levels of humanin and SHMOOSE, tiny proteins made by mitochondria. These proteins have been linked to protection against heart disease, Alzheimer's disease, and age-related damage.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a possible biological reason why a Mediterranean diet is linked to healthier ageing of the heart and brain.
ai.life_skill: Try eating more Mediterranean-style foods such as vegetables, fruits, wholegrains, nuts, and olive oil.
ai.fact: Humanin and SHMOOSE are tiny proteins produced by mitochondria and have been linked to protection against heart disease, Alzheimer's disease, and age-related damage.

quiz.question: Which diet was linked to higher levels of humanin and SHMOOSE in older adults?
quiz.answer: Older adults who closely followed the Mediterranean diet had higher levels of these proteins.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study, so it cannot prove the diet caused the higher protein levels.

items.title: Can psychedelics soothe an overactive immune system? New meta-analysis investigates

ai.headline: A review suggests psychedelics may affect inflammation and immune responses.
ai.summary: Researchers carried out a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on serotonergic psychedelics such as psilocybin and LSD. They focused on whether these substances have anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating properties.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows scientists are exploring whether drugs known for changing mood and perception might also influence the immune system.
ai.fact: Serotonergic psychedelics such as psilocybin and LSD are being studied for anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating effects.

quiz.question: What did the researchers review psychedelics for?
quiz.answer: They reviewed their anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating properties.

ai.caveat: A single review does not prove psychedelics can treat immune-related conditions.

items.title: Predicting alcohol consumption from resting-state functional connectivity: Feature relevance and the potential of meta-matching.

ai.headline: Brain scans show only weak links between resting brain activity and drinking habits
ai.summary: Researchers used brain scans and machine learning to see if resting-state brain connectivity could predict alcohol consumption scores in 739 people. Both models predicted scores only weakly but significantly, and the brain patterns were only partly reliable across groups.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that brain imaging may hint at drinking-related patterns but is not yet accurate enough to predict individual behaviour.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your own drinking habits affect your wellbeing rather than relying on brain scans to judge risk.
ai.fact: Resting-state functional connectivity contains weak but reproducible signals linked to alcohol consumption scores.

quiz.question: How well did the brain-scan models predict alcohol consumption scores?
quiz.answer: They predicted scores only weakly but significantly, with a correlation of about 0.15.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the predictive link was weak, so it cannot be used to judge individual risk.

items.title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial

ai.headline: Durvalumab plus chemotherapy before surgery helped most patients with early-stage lung cancer proceed to surgery.
ai.summary: The study tested durvalumab plus chemotherapy given before surgery in people with resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer. Most patients were able to have surgery, with encouraging rates of complete cancer cell disappearance in removed tissue, and continuing treatment with chemoradiotherapy plus durvalumab raised no new safety concerns for those whose tumours remained unresectable.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how combining immunotherapy with chemotherapy may improve treatment options for people with early-stage lung cancer.
ai.fact: Neoadjuvant treatment means therapy given before the main treatment, such as surgery.

quiz.question: What happened for most patients in the trial after receiving durvalumab plus chemotherapy before surgery?
quiz.answer: Most patients were able to proceed to surgery.

ai.caveat: This is a single phase 2 trial, so the results are encouraging but not yet definitive proof.

items.title: New evidence suggests spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater

ai.headline: New analysis suggests Spinosaurus was mostly aquatic, while some marine reptiles spent time on land.
ai.summary: Yale scientists used machine learning on thousands of fossil measurements to study how prehistoric animals adapted to water. The findings indicate Spinosaurus likely spent most of its life underwater, whereas some ancient marine reptiles previously thought to be fully aquatic actually spent considerable time on land.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that evolutionary paths are not always one-way streets, as animals can return to aquatic lifestyles after living on land for millions of years.
ai.life_skill: Notice that initial assumptions about a category (like 'marine reptile') might be wrong when new data is applied.
ai.fact: Spinosaurus is suggested to have spent most of its life underwater, unlike some other marine reptiles that spent time on land.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about some ancient marine reptiles?
quiz.answer: Some ancient marine reptiles previously thought to be fully aquatic actually spent considerable time on land.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a study, so the specific methodological details and peer-review status of the original Yale research are not provided here.

items.title: [Correspondence] Beyond imaging thresholds in large-core stroke thrombectomy – Authors’ reply
authors: Amrou Sarraj, Vincet Costalat, Osama O Zaidat, Shinichi Yoshimura, Zhongrong Miao, Martin Bendszus, ATLAS investigators

ai.headline: Stroke experts disagree with commentary on imaging thresholds for large-core clot removal.
ai.summary: The authors are replying to a commentary on their ATLAS meta-analysis about removing clots in large-core strokes. They say the commentary’s ideas are worth considering, but they disagree with the treatment conclusions drawn from them. This reply does not present new study results.

quiz.question: What do the authors say about the commentary on their stroke meta-analysis?

items.title: What are microchimeric cells doing to our brain?

ai.headline: Cells exchanged during pregnancy can live in the brain and might affect health or behaviour.
ai.summary: The article explores microchimeric cells—cells exchanged during pregnancy—that can take up residency in the brain. It asks whether these cells could influence development, health, or behaviour. It does not report results from a specific study.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a cellular legacy from pregnancy may remain in the brain, which could change how we understand lifelong health.
ai.fact: Cells exchanged during pregnancy can take up residency in the human brain.

quiz.question: Where can cells exchanged during pregnancy take up residency?
quiz.answer: They can take up residency in the brain.

ai.caveat: This is a news column that poses questions rather than presenting tested research findings.

items.title: How much development aid is spent on climate change?

ai.headline: One-fifth of aid spent on climate
ai.summary: Researchers studied development aid spending, finding around one-fifth is spent on climate-related projects, which may impact other aid projects. The study aims to understand what climate-related aid means and its potential effects. The findings have implications for aid allocation and prioritization.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding aid spending on climate change matters for everyday life as it affects global efforts to address environmental issues.

ai.fact: Around one-fifth of development aid is spent on climate-related projects.

quiz.question: What proportion of development aid is spent on climate-related projects?
quiz.answer: Around one-fifth of development aid is spent on climate-related projects.

items.title: Watch the universe emerge from the dark ages, with Lumina

ai.headline: Universe simulation tracks first 2 billion years
ai.summary: Researchers created a simulation called Lumina to track the universe's development. The simulation follows dark matter, galaxies, stars, and cosmic structures. It provides greater detail and volume than previous simulations.
ai.why_it_matters: This simulation helps us better understand the universe's early development and formation of cosmic structures.
ai.fact: The universe's first 2 billion years are a crucial period for its development.

quiz.question: What does the Lumina simulation track?
quiz.answer: The Lumina simulation tracks dark matter, galaxies, stars, and cosmic structures over the universe's first 2 billion years.

items.title: Fibromyalgia in pregnancy and postpartum period: effects on quality of life, obstetric outcomes, delivery decisions, and breastfeeding: a systematic review.
items.venue: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
authors: Liana Maria Tôrres de Araújo Azi

ai.headline: Fibromyalgia affects pregnancy outcomes
ai.summary: Researchers studied the impact of fibromyalgia on pregnancy and postpartum health. They found that fibromyalgia is linked to reduced quality of life and higher rates of depressive symptoms. Fibromyalgia may also increase obstetric risks, such as gestational diabetes and preterm birth.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the effects of fibromyalgia on pregnancy and postpartum health can help improve care for women with the condition
ai.life_skill: Check with your healthcare provider if you have fibromyalgia and are pregnant or planning to become pregnant
ai.fact: Fibromyalgia is associated with greater pain intensity and reduced functional capacity during pregnancy

quiz.question: What is the impact of fibromyalgia on quality of life during pregnancy?
quiz.answer: Fibromyalgia is linked to reduced quality of life during pregnancy

items.title: The AI Paradox: How Optimization May Undermine Meaningful Work in Helping Professions

ai.headline: AI may undermine meaningful work
ai.summary: Researchers studied the impact of AI on helping professions, finding that automation may concentrate on tasks that give workers a sense of meaning. The study used a combination of surveys and analysis of online forum posts to understand how workers perceive meaningful work. The results suggest that optimization, rather than AI itself, may be the main risk to meaningful work.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it challenges the assumption that AI will free up workers to focus on more meaningful tasks, and instead suggests that AI may undermine the very tasks that give work meaning.
ai.life_skill: Notice how automation affects your sense of purpose at work
ai.fact: Meaningful work is often concentrated in tasks that are increasingly automatable

quiz.question: What is the main risk to meaningful work according to the study?
quiz.answer: Optimization, rather than AI itself, is the main risk to meaningful work.

items.title: Sarcopenia Is Associated With Severe Treatment Toxicity and Mortality in Older Adults With Advanced Cancer: A Secondary Analysis
items.venue: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle

ai.headline: Older adults with advanced cancer who have sarcopenia face higher severe treatment toxicity and lower one-year survival.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed 161 people aged 70 or older starting new cancer treatment. Those with sarcopenia—low muscle strength plus low muscle quantity—were more likely to have severe non-blood toxicities and had worse one-year survival than those without sarcopenia. Muscle quantity alone was not significantly linked to these outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that checking both muscle strength and quantity may help identify older cancer patients at higher risk from treatment.
ai.life_skill: If you or someone you know is an older adult starting cancer treatment, ask the care team about assessing muscle strength as well as muscle quantity.
ai.fact: Sarcopenia means a loss of muscle strength, quantity and performance, mainly from ageing or disease.
ai.caveat: This was a secondary analysis of one trial’s usual-care arm, mostly non-Hispanic white participants, so results may not apply to everyone.

items.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios

ai.headline: Genetic scores linked to education are also linked to children's mental health within families.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study. They found that both cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores were associated with externalising behaviour, such as hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, such as anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that genetic factors linked to schooling are connected to mental health in complex ways within families.
ai.life_skill: Notice that behaviour and mood are influenced by many factors, not just school performance.
ai.fact: Education-related polygenic scores are associated with both externalising and internalising behaviour in youth.

quiz.question: What did the study find about education-related polygenic scores and youth mental health?
quiz.answer: They were associated with both externalising behaviour, such as hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, such as anxiety and low mood.

items.title: Parental Dementia History is Associated with Peripheral Immune Aging Rather than Generalized Biological and Brain Age Acceleration in Midlife

ai.headline: Having a parent with dementia is linked to immune cell changes in midlife, not faster brain or general biological aging.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 1,204 middle-aged adults and found that parental dementia history was linked to an expansion of CD8 memory T cells and shorter telomeres, but not to accelerated epigenetic or brain aging. Earlier parental dementia onset was linked to a faster pace of biological aging, while poorer parental cognitive performance was linked to faster epigenetic aging and a larger brain age gap.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that family dementia risk may show up in the immune system during midlife, offering a possible early clue before brain changes appear.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether close relatives developed dementia early or had memory problems, and mention this to a healthcare professional if you are concerned about your own risk.
ai.fact: Parental dementia history was associated with CD8 memory T cell expansion in midlife adults.

quiz.question: What did the study find about parental dementia history and brain aging in midlife adults?
quiz.answer: Parental dementia history was not associated with accelerated brain aging.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that parental dementia causes immune aging.

items.title: Sex and Subsistence: Income Effects on Risky Sexual Behavior and Partner Selection -- by Natalie Bau, Corinne Low, Bryce Steinberg

ai.headline: Giving female university students monthly cash reduced risky sex and improved partner choice in Zambia.
ai.summary: Researchers ran a randomised trial giving monthly cash assistance to female students at the University of Zambia and tracked their sexual behaviour. Women receiving cash were less likely to have sex, used condoms more often, and those who were not sexually active at the start were much less likely to begin having sex; among those who did have sex, partner quality improved.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that financial insecurity can shape sexual decisions and partner selection, suggesting income support may help reduce risky sexual behaviour.
ai.life_skill: Notice how money worries might influence your own choices in relationships and consider seeking support if finances are affecting your wellbeing.
ai.fact: A temporary increase in income was linked to less sex, less condomless sex, and better partner quality among female university students in Zambia.

quiz.question: What happened to sexual activity among women who were not sexually at baseline when they received cash assistance?
quiz.answer: The likelihood of having sex fell by 43%.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings come from one setting in Zambia, so they may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning

ai.headline: AI agents can improve over time by jointly learning from past memories and reusable skills.
ai.summary: The study tested MemCryst, a framework where an AI agent stores past experiences as memory and turns repeated patterns into skills. Across ten settings including robot control, reading, conversation, maths and code, using memory and skills together performed better than using either alone in seven comparisons.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI assistants might get better at everyday tasks by learning from experience without needing their core model rewritten.

ai.fact: On ALFWorld, joint memory-and-skill serving reached 63.17% success versus 59.83% memory-only and 50.50% skill-only.

quiz.question: What did MemCryst use together to help an AI agent solve tasks?

items.title: Healing campuses: Implementing Nature-Based Interventions to Promote University Student Mental Health and Wellbeing

ai.headline: Nature-based activities on university campuses may improve student mental health and wellbeing.
ai.summary: A review of eleven trials across five countries looked at nature-based interventions such as forest therapy, outdoor mindfulness and therapeutic horticulture. These activities were linked to lower stress, anxiety and depressive symptoms, better mood, attention and wellbeing, and greater connection to nature.

items.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training

ai.headline: A simple AI recipe can teach a humanoid robot to box in about seven minutes of single-GPU training, using a pretrained controller.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the results come from simulated boxing experiments rather than a physical robot.

ai.fact: Higher NEFL levels were associated with poorer global cognition and delayed memory in this study.

ai.why_it_matters: It shows that popular health apps and AI tools are not yet proven to improve serious health outcomes for older people with long-term conditions.
ai.life_skill: Check with a qualified healthcare professional before relying on a digital or AI medication tool to manage your medicines.
ai.fact: Nineteen randomised trials were reviewed, but only six could be combined in the statistical analysis.

quiz.question: Did the review find that digital or AI medication management clearly reduces hospitalisation or death in older adults with chronic disease?
quiz.answer: No, the two studies reporting these outcomes did not show a clear benefit.

ai.caveat: The evidence is limited by highly mixed results and too few high-quality trials to pool most outcomes reliably.

items.title: A systematic review of the effectiveness of interventions to promote employment rates among people with disabilities in the UK between 2009 and 2024

ai.headline: Voluntary, clinically integrated employment support may help people with disabilities find work, but evidence is limited.
ai.summary: This preprint systematic review looked at UK studies from 2009 to 2024 on employment programmes for people with disabilities. It found promising results for voluntary, clinically integrated support such as Individual Placement and Support and co-located Employment Advisers, while mandatory Jobcentre programmes showed no significant gains, but most studies were small and local.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which kinds of employment support are linked to better job outcomes for people with disabilities, while highlighting where more research is needed.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether employment support is voluntary and linked to health services before deciding to take part.
ai.fact: The UK disability employment gap is 30 percentage points and health-related economic inactivity costs an estimated £212 billion annually.

quiz.question: What did the review find about mandatory Jobcentre programmes?
quiz.answer: They showed no significant employment gains.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and the included studies were localised and may not apply across all UK labour markets.

ai.headline: A systematic review finds limited mental health research for children and adolescents in Mozambique, with some clinical data and few tested tools or interventions.

items.title: Immune Thrombocytopenia in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.

ai.headline: Immune thrombocytopenia in low- and middle-income countries differs from high-income settings and needs tailored care.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 20 studies looked at adult immune thrombocytopenia in low- and middle-income countries. items.title: Loneliness in Older Adults is Associated with Altered Frontolimbic Connectivity During Negative Emotional Processing and Increased Depression Vulnerability

items.title: From clinician review to measurable human oversight of AI-drafted paediatric discharge documents

ai.headline: AI-drafted children's discharge letters were understood as well as standard ones, but clinicians missed some errors.

items.title: Access to and control over water security: The perspective of gender equality in Lao PDR

ai.headline: Women in rural Laos collect most household water but have little say in water decisions.
ai.summary: Researchers held focus groups and interviews across eight villages and government levels in Lao PDR. They found that women and girls mainly collect household water, yet women are underrepresented in water supply decision-making at household, community and institutional levels.

ai.fact: In Lao PDR, women and children, particularly daughters, are primarily responsible for household water collection despite limited participation in water governance.

quiz.answer: Women and children, particularly daughters, are primarily responsible for household water collection.

items.title: Maternal Anxiety and Depression, Parenting, and Child Social-Emotional Functioning as an Interconnected System: Network Evidence from Born in Bradford

ai.headline: Maternal anxiety linked to child behaviour
ai.summary: Researchers studied the relationship between maternal emotional wellbeing and child social-emotional functioning in 5,143 mother-child dyads. ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the interconnectedness of maternal symptoms, parenting, and child functioning can inform more effective interventions for families.

ai.fact: Maternal anxiety and depression are closely related to child social-emotional functioning.

quiz.answer: A shared family-focused approach that supports parental worry and child conduct problems.

items.title: “There is nothing fake about the harm”: The lived experiences and impacts of sexualized deepfake abuse

ai.headline: Sexualized deepfake abuse causes serious harm, including unique struggles over authenticity and credibility.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 25 Australian adults, 15 victim-survivors and 10 perpetrators, about sexualized deepfake abuse. items.title: Interprofessional education in palliative care: a theory-informed evaluation of a storyline-based curriculum for health and social care students

ai.headline: A small palliative-care course helped health and social care students learn teamwork and reflect on their professional roles using stories.
ai.summary: Researchers evaluated a storyline-based interprofessional palliative care course with 25 students from medicine, nursing, social work, and religious education at one German university. quiz.answer: They rated social and communication skills, knowledge of other professional groups, and team-oriented problem solving especially positively.

items.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems

ai.headline: AI agents can accidentally reveal secrets by combining harmless pieces of information they find online.
ai.summary: Researchers tested AI agents that read documents and answer questions. Even when questions seemed safe, the agents sometimes combined details from different documents to reveal confidential information, despite safeguards like warning labels and rules against sharing.

ai.fact: AI agents can disclose sensitive conclusions by piecing together separate pieces of information, even when each piece seems harmless on its own.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find about AI agents and confidential information?
quiz.answer: AI agents sometimes combined separate pieces of information to reveal confidential conclusions, even when questions seemed safe and safeguards were in place.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the results come from simulated and live agent tests rather than real-world use.

ai.summary: Researchers studied the relationship between motivation and reading comprehension in 3390 Dutch 15-year-olds. items.title: Association Between Exercise and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) Levels in Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

items.title: Psychoeducation for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults: a systematic review of formats and delivery approaches

items.title: Role of Nutrition Therapy in Prediabetes: A Systematic Review

ai.headline: Structured diets may improve blood sugar and weight in adults with prediabetes, but no single diet is best.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at ten randomised trials involving 1,098 adults with prediabetes. ai.caveat: The review included only ten small, varied trials with some risk-of-bias concerns, so the findings are not definitive.

items.title: Genetic diversity must underpin area-based conservation and restoration targets

items.title: The association between orthorexia nervosa and social media use: A systematic review and meta-analysis

items.title: What the submission does not show: Complexifying cognitive offloading in students' mathematical work with LLMs

ai.headline: A student's final maths answer does not show whether they used an LLM to do the thinking for them.

items.title: Multi-agent LLM diagnostic teams improve differential recall on curated cases and reverse on real emergency notes: a label-level reversal without a clinician-judged safety difference

items.title: Olfactory combinatorial coding supports risk–reward decision-making in Caenorhabditis elegans
