items.title: Physical exercise and lower psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescents in China: evidence from a moderated serial mediation model

items.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models

ai.headline: AI models learn to write “wait” from training data, not just from reinforcement learning.
ai.summary: The study traced how the word “wait” appears in AI reasoning models. It found that reinforcement learning rarely invents the word from scratch; instead, models usually inherit it from their training data or fine-tuning, and RL often just increases how often it is used.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and is based on sampled outputs from open models rather than a general proof about all AI systems.

items.title: Combining Dispositional and Behavioural Facets of SRL, and the Role of Students' Growth Orientation

items.title: Association of childhood mild traumatic brain injury with mental and behavioral health outcomes later in life among U.S. Veterans: A LIMBIC-CENC study

ai.headline: Childhood mild head injuries are linked to worse mental health in US Veterans later in life.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 1,286 US Veterans and found that 61.3% had a childhood mild traumatic brain injury. Those with a childhood injury had higher scores for PTSD, anger, depression, anxiety, emotional-behavioural dyscontrol, sleep problems and neurobehavioural symptoms, and lower life satisfaction and resilience, after adjusting for demographic, behavioural and military history factors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that health markers present before military service may be linked to later mental wellbeing, which could help providers offer earlier support.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether a past childhood head injury might be relevant when seeking mental health support, and discuss it with a qualified professional.
ai.fact: Among Veterans with childhood mTBI, multiple injuries were linked to worse outcomes, while physical activity and higher education were linked to better outcomes.

quiz.question: What did the study find about Veterans with a childhood mild traumatic brain injury compared with those without one?
quiz.answer: They had higher scores for PTSD, anger, depression, anxiety, emotional-behavioural dyscontrol, sleep problems and neurobehavioural symptoms, and lower life satisfaction and resilience.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional observational study, so it cannot show that childhood head injury caused the later outcomes.

items.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration

ai.headline: AI learns efficient exploration
ai.summary: Researchers studied sequential decision-making under partial observability and proposed a framework called ASTEROID. They found that ASTEROID achieves higher returns and uses fewer interactions than reinforcement learning baselines. The framework enables efficient test-time exploration in various environments, including robotic manipulation and navigation.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it could lead to more efficient and effective decision-making in complex, real-world situations
ai.life_skill: Try to systematically gather information before making decisions
ai.fact: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is a challenging problem in artificial intelligence

quiz.question: What is the name of the proposed framework?
quiz.answer: ASTEROID

ai.caveat: The findings are based on a preprint and have not been peer-reviewed, so the results should be interpreted with caution

items.title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation

ai.headline: New method improves question generation
ai.summary: Researchers studied on-policy distillation and introduced a framework called Ask-to-Distill to generate valuable questions for distillation. The method optimizes question generation without access to correct answers. It improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery in various tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it can enhance the efficiency of knowledge transfer and learning in artificial intelligence systems
ai.life_skill: Try to ask targeted and diverse questions to improve learning outcomes
ai.fact: On-policy distillation can succeed with surprisingly few training questions

quiz.question: What is the main goal of the Ask-to-Distill framework?
quiz.answer: The main goal is to generate valuable questions for on-policy distillation without access to correct answers.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on a preprint and have not been peer-reviewed, so the results should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Validating OpenCap Kinematics for ACL Injury-Related Movements In and Out of the Lab

ai.headline: A smartphone app can measure ACL injury risk movement scores in the lab, but results differ outside it.
ai.summary: Researchers compared smartphone-based OpenCap software with standard lab motion capture in 26 female athletes doing jumping and cutting tasks. In the lab, the app’s kAIR injury-risk score closely matched the lab system, but scores taken outside the lab only moderately matched in-lab scores.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how portable phone tools might one day help track movement-related injury risk outside specialist labs, though the method still needs more testing.
ai.life_skill: Notice how you land and change direction during sport, and ask a qualified coach or physiotherapist about safer movement habits.
ai.fact: ACL injuries are common in adolescent female athletes and can affect long-term health.

quiz.question: How did OpenCap’s in-lab kAIR scores compare with standard lab motion capture?
quiz.answer: They were strongly correlated and showed good agreement.

ai.caveat: This is a small preprint (not yet peer reviewed) with 26 athletes, so the findings are preliminary and not proof.

items.title: Ocular Phototherapy and Mental Health: What Vision Scientists and Clinicians Need to Know

ai.headline: Bright light therapy can help depression, but the right dose depends on light colour, eye exposure and age.
ai.summary: The review examined how bright light therapy works for seasonal and non-seasonal depression through light-sensitive cells in the eye. It found that blue-appearing light works better than dim red light for seasonal affective disorder but has not beaten ordinary white light, and that the amount of light reaching the retina roughly halves between ages 25 and 75.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that light therapy is a real, low-cost option for some mood problems, but its effects depend on physical details like spectrum and age rather than brightness alone.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the light you use for mood support is bright white and reaches your eyes, rather than assuming any lamp will work.
ai.fact: Melanopsin-expressing retinal ganglion cells help light influence circadian and mood-related brain regions.

quiz.question: Has blue-appearing light been shown to outperform broadband white light for seasonal affective disorder?
quiz.answer: No, it has not outperformed broadband white light.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review and preprint, not peer-reviewed evidence, so its conclusions are not yet confirmed.

items.title: From Thriving to Stressing: Distinct Roles of Autonomy Satisfaction and Frustration in Adolescents' Learning Behaviors and Academic Outcomes

ai.headline: Feeling in control of your choices helps teens study better and feel less burned out, while feeling controlled does the opposite.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 1,639 10th-grade students in China about whether they felt their autonomy was supported or blocked, and linked this to their study habits, exam results and school burnout. Students who felt autonomy satisfaction showed more persistence, less procrastination, better achievement and less burnout; autonomy frustration showed the reverse pattern. The protective effects on persistence and procrastination were stronger for boys.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that whether teenagers feel they have a say in their learning is linked to both how well they do at school and how stressed they feel.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you feel pressured or forced in your schoolwork and look for small ways to make your own choices about how to approach it.
ai.fact: Autonomy satisfaction and autonomy frustration are separate experiences that predict different academic and well-being outcomes.

quiz.question: What did autonomy frustration predict in the study?
quiz.answer: Autonomy frustration predicted lower persistence, higher procrastination, poorer achievement and increased school burnout.

ai.caveat: This was a single observational study in one region of China, so it shows links rather than proof that autonomy causes these outcomes, and results may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: An AI tool improves weather forecasts up to a month ahead

ai.headline: AI improves weather forecasts
ai.summary: Researchers developed an AI tool to enhance weather forecasting. The tool improves forecasts of precipitation, temperature, and pressure 3-5 weeks in advance. It refines both physics- and AI-based weather models.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because accurate long-term weather forecasts can help people prepare for extreme weather events
ai.life_skill: Check weather forecasts regularly to plan ahead
ai.fact: AI can improve weather forecasting up to a month ahead

quiz.question: What time range does the AI tool improve weather forecasts for?
quiz.answer: 3-5 weeks in advance

ai.caveat: The study's findings are based on a single innovative application and may not be universally applicable

items.title: Green transition provides a crucial opportunity to finance universal health coverage
authors: Judite Goncalves, Fernando Postali, Moh Shadiqur Rahman, Christopher Millett

ai.headline: Ending fossil fuel subsidies and taxing carbon could raise money for universal health coverage in poorer countries.
ai.summary: The paper looks at how the shift to green energy could create new government revenue in low and middle income countries by cutting fossil fuel subsidies, introducing carbon pricing, and collecting royalties from critical minerals. It argues health systems have a strong claim to some of this money because they deal with the health effects of fossil fuels and mining, though how much reaches those most in need depends on politics and governance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how climate policy and health funding are connected, and why decisions about energy money affect whether people can access healthcare.
ai.life_skill: Notice how government spending choices link energy, environment, and health in your own country.
ai.fact: Fossil fuel subsidies can account for a large proportion of government spending in low and middle income countries.

quiz.question: What does the paper say determines how much new green-transition money reaches people in greatest need?
quiz.answer: Political decisions and good governance.

ai.caveat: This is a commentary based on reasoning rather than a study measuring actual outcomes, so the claims are not proven.

items.title: Four questions about schoolwork feedback to guide young students' learning

ai.headline: Feedback that focuses on effort and strategy helps young students learn better than feedback about fixed ability.
ai.summary: The article discusses how adults respond when a young student gets a low math score, contrasting comments that suggest fixed ability, such as saying math is not their strength, with feedback that labels work as careless. It suggests that feedback should guide students toward learning strategies and effort rather than fixed traits.
ai.why_it_matters: The way adults give feedback can shape whether a young person believes they can improve or feels stuck.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether feedback focuses on fixed ability or on effort and strategy, and ask for comments that suggest how to improve.
ai.fact: Feedback that attributes results to effort or strategy can support learning more than feedback that attributes results to fixed ability.

quiz.question: What kind of feedback does the article suggest is more helpful for a student who gets a low math score?
quiz.answer: Feedback that focuses on effort and learning strategies rather than fixed ability.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed study, so it does not provide direct evidence of effects or outcomes.

items.title: Motor unit mechanisms of speed control in mouse locomotion

ai.headline: Mouse elbow muscles use different motor units at different walking speeds, mainly by recruiting more units rather than firing them faster.
ai.summary: Researchers recorded individual motor units in two elbow muscles of mice while they walked at different speeds. They found activity differed between muscles, units were recruited only on some strides, and faster walking mainly involved recruiting more units rather than increasing firing rates.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how the nervous system flexibly controls movement speed, which helps scientists understand how bodies coordinate muscles during everyday actions like walking.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your arm muscles feel different when you move slowly versus quickly.
ai.fact: Motor units are groups of muscle fibres controlled by a single motor neuron.

quiz.question: What changed more when mice walked faster: recruitment probability or firing rate?
quiz.answer: Recruitment probability increased proportionally more than firing rate.

ai.caveat: This is a single study in mice, so the findings may not apply directly to humans.

items.title: Half-matched bone marrow transplant expands options for children with severe aplastic anemia

ai.headline: Half-matched bone marrow transplants helped 96% of young patients with severe aplastic anemia survive.
ai.summary: Researchers studied bone marrow transplants using half-matched family donors in children, adolescents and young adults with severe aplastic anemia. The approach achieved a 96% survival rate and expands access to potentially curative treatment for patients without a fully matched donor.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows more young people with a rare, life-threatening blood disorder may have a curative treatment option even without a perfectly matched donor.
ai.life_skill: If you or a family member has severe aplastic anemia, ask a qualified transplant specialist whether a half-matched family donor could be an option.
ai.fact: Half-matched family donor bone marrow transplants achieved a 96% survival rate in young patients with severe aplastic anemia.

quiz.question: What survival rate did half-matched family donor transplants achieve in young patients with severe aplastic anemia?
quiz.answer: The approach achieved a 96% survival rate.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed study, so the finding should be treated as preliminary until full research is published.

items.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars

ai.headline: Astronauts' hearts adapt to space travel
ai.summary: Researchers studied 13 astronauts in space, finding their hearts adapted to weightlessness and Martian gravity. The astronauts' hearts handled months of weightlessness without major problems. Regular exercise during spaceflight helped with heart adaptation.
ai.why_it_matters: This finding matters for planning future long-duration space missions, like to Mars.
ai.life_skill: Try regular exercise to improve heart health
ai.fact: The human heart can adapt to weightlessness and Martian gravity with regular exercise

quiz.question: What helped astronauts' hearts adapt to space travel?
quiz.answer: Regular exercise helped astronauts' hearts adapt to space travel.

ai.caveat: This study had a small sample size of 13 astronauts, so more research is needed to confirm the findings.

items.title: Massive study of 460,000 people challenges ultra-processed food cancer fears

ai.headline: Ultra-processed foods were not linked to higher colorectal cancer risk overall in a large US study.
ai.summary: Researchers studied more than 460,000 Americans and found no overall association between ultra-processed foods and colorectal cancer risk. Processed meat was linked to higher cancer incidence, while ultra-processed whole grains and dairy were linked to lower incidence.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that not all ultra-processed foods carry the same cancer risk, so blanket fears may be too simple.
ai.life_skill: Check food labels for processed meat rather than avoiding all ultra-processed foods.
ai.fact: Processed meat was linked to higher colorectal cancer incidence in this study.

quiz.question: What did the study find about ultra-processed foods and colorectal cancer risk overall?
quiz.answer: They were not associated with increased colorectal cancer risk overall.

ai.caveat: As an observational study, it can show links but cannot prove that ultra-processed foods cause or prevent cancer.

items.title: Video Images About Decisions for Ethical Outcomes in the Emergency Department (VIDEO-ED)

ai.headline: A video decision aid trial in emergency departments aims to improve advance care planning documentation.
ai.summary: This randomised trial tested whether showing patients video images about decisions for ethical outcomes in the emergency department improves advance care planning documentation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how simple tools might help people record their healthcare wishes in urgent settings.
ai.life_skill: Try thinking ahead about your healthcare preferences and discussing them with loved ones.
ai.fact: Advance care planning documentation records a person’s healthcare wishes for future treatment decisions.

quiz.question: What type of study was used to test the video decision aid?
quiz.answer: It was a randomised controlled trial.

ai.caveat: The abstract does not report whether the video actually improved documentation or any results from the trial.

items.title: From Politics to Process: Evidence from Progressive Era Naturalizations -- by Abhay Aneja, Guo Xu

ai.headline: Standardizing procedures reduces bias
ai.summary: Researchers studied the introduction of federal standards for citizenship applications in the US. They found that standardizing procedures reduced political bias in naturalization practices. This change also affected the composition of new citizens.
ai.why_it_matters: This study matters because it shows how standardizing administrative procedures can reduce politically-biased policy implementation in everyday life
ai.life_skill: Try to understand how rules and procedures can impact fairness in decision-making
ai.fact: Standardizing administrative procedures can discipline politically-biased policy implementation

quiz.question: What happened to naturalization practices after the introduction of federal standards?
quiz.answer: Naturalization practices converged across cities and the electoral cycle disappeared

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution

items.title: Inside the science of the ‘robo ump’ revolutionizing baseball

ai.headline: Robo ump revolutionizes baseball
ai.summary: Researchers are refining an automated ball-strike system using high-speed cameras and a pitch cannon. The system is about to call its first World Series. The technology aims to improve accuracy in baseball games.
ai.why_it_matters: This technology could change the way sports games are officiated, potentially reducing human error and controversy.
ai.fact: High-speed cameras and automated systems can be used to improve accuracy in sports officiating.

quiz.question: What technology is being used to refine the automated ball-strike system?
quiz.answer: High-speed cameras and a pitch cannon.

ai.caveat: This is a news report and not a peer-reviewed study, so the findings and implications may not be thoroughly validated.

items.title: Daraxonrasib in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer

ai.headline: Daraxonrasib treats metastatic pancreatic cancer
ai.summary: Researchers studied Daraxonrasib in patients with previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, finding its effects. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. The treatment's outcomes were reported.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters for understanding new treatments for pancreatic cancer.
ai.fact: Daraxonrasib is a treatment for metastatic pancreatic cancer.

quiz.question: What type of cancer was treated with Daraxonrasib?
quiz.answer: Metastatic pancreatic cancer.

ai.caveat: The study's findings may not be generalizable to all patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Nutritional Supplements in the Treatment of Endometriosis-Associated Symptoms: A Systematic Review

ai.headline: Some supplements may ease endometriosis pain and quality of life, but evidence is too weak for routine use.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 24 randomised trials involving 2,019 women with endometriosis to test dietary supplements against placebo, no treatment, or standard care. Pain and quality-of-life results were mixed; specially formulated curcumin, selenium added to hormone treatment, Proscur, and garlic showed some benefit, while omega-3, conventional curcumin, and resveratrol did not. Fertility measures improved in some studies but did not lead to higher pregnancy rates.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people with endometriosis understand which supplements might help symptoms and that they should not replace standard medical care.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a qualified healthcare professional before taking any supplement for endometriosis symptoms.
ai.fact: Some trials reported that nanomicellar curcumin or selenium added to dienogest improved pain or quality of life in women with endometriosis.

quiz.question: Did fertility-related improvements in the reviewed trials lead to higher pregnancy rates?
quiz.answer: No, improvements in some fertility measures did not lead to higher pregnancy rates.

ai.caveat: The review found mixed results and concluded that evidence remains insufficient to support routine use of supplements as standalone treatments.

items.title: Antidepressant effects of artemisinin and its derivatives: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled animal studies.

ai.headline: Artemisinin reduced depression-like behaviors in rodent studies, but the evidence is very uncertain.
ai.summary: Researchers combined 17 randomized controlled animal studies involving 402 rodents to test artemisinin and its derivatives in depression models. Artemisinin reduced immobility in forced swim and tail suspension tests, increased sucrose preference, eased anxiety-like behaviors, and improved cognitive performance compared with controls.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how early animal research can point toward possible future treatments, but does not yet prove anything for people.
ai.fact: Artemisinin and its derivatives reduced depression-like and anxiety-like behaviors and improved cognitive performance in rodent models of depression.

quiz.question: What did the review find about artemisinin in rodent depression models?
quiz.answer: It reduced immobility in forced swim and tail suspension tests, increased sucrose preference, eased anxiety-like behaviors, and improved cognitive performance compared with controls.

ai.caveat: The evidence was rated very low certainty because of high risk of bias, substantial heterogeneity, and indirectness from animal studies to humans.

items.title: How AI threat perception relates to post-adoptive AI agent engagement: the dual paths of self-efficacy and defensive motivation

ai.headline: AI threat perception affects engagement
ai.summary: This study examined how AI threat perception relates to post-adoptive AI agent engagement. It found that AI threat perception is indirectly associated with engagement through self-efficacy and defensive motivation. The study also identified demographic and contextual factors that influence this relationship.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how AI threat perception affects engagement is crucial for effective human-agent collaboration in the workplace
ai.life_skill: Try to develop your self-efficacy when working with AI agents
ai.fact: AI threat perception is linked to post-adoptive AI agent engagement through self-efficacy and defensive motivation

quiz.question: What is the relationship between AI threat perception and post-adoptive AI agent engagement?
quiz.answer: AI threat perception is indirectly associated with engagement through self-efficacy and defensive motivation

ai.caveat: This study is cross-sectional, so it does not establish causation or temporal dynamics

items.title: Variation in psychiatric diagnoses and use of psychotropic medication among children, adolescents, and young adults in Denmark

ai.headline: Psychiatric diagnoses and medication use rose among young people in Denmark from 2010 to 2025, with wide local differences.
ai.summary: Researchers used national health registers to look at all Danish residents aged 0-24 from 2010 to 2025. They found that diagnoses such as ADHD and autism spectrum disorders, and use of medicines such as melatonin and sertraline, increased over time, and rates varied across regions and municipalities.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that where a young person lives may be linked to how likely they are to receive a psychiatric diagnosis or medication, which matters for understanding fairness in healthcare.
ai.life_skill: Notice that diagnosis and medication rates can differ by area, and discuss any concerns about diagnosis or treatment with a qualified healthcare professional.
ai.fact: In Denmark, the annual prevalence of ADHD among people aged 0-24 rose from 0.41 to 2.3 per 100 individuals between 2010 and 2025.

quiz.question: What did the study find about geographic variation in psychiatric diagnoses and medication use?
quiz.answer: There was marked geographic variation across regions, health councils, and municipalities for diagnoses and psychotropic medications.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and descriptive register data cannot establish the causes of the observed increases or geographic variation.

items.title: Extracurricular Participation and Student-Reported Opportunity Constraints in an Urban Moroccan Secondary School: An Exploratory Study

ai.headline: Many Moroccan secondary students want extracurricular activities but face barriers like lack of time and too few options.
ai.summary: An exploratory questionnaire study of 100 students at one urban upper-secondary school in Fez, Morocco, looked at extracurricular participation, barriers, and perceived outcomes. Forty-five percent reported no participation, and lack of time and scarcity of activities were the most commonly reported barriers; participation frequency was linked to perceived academic improvement and stress relief in the full sample, but these links disappeared when only participants were analysed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that offering activities is not the same as students being able to take part, which matters for understanding how school enrichment actually reaches young people.
ai.life_skill: Notice what stops you from joining activities you are interested in and see if any barrier can be changed.
ai.fact: In this study, 45% of students reported no extracurricular participation and 32% participated only once or twice per year.

quiz.question: What happened to the link between participation frequency and perceived academic improvement when the analysis was limited to students who took part in any activities?
quiz.answer: The association was no longer statistically significant.

ai.caveat: This is a single, small, cross-sectional preprint from one school, so it cannot show cause and effect and may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Cognitive effects of untreated unilateral and bilateral hearing loss in midlife: Preliminary evidence

ai.headline: Middle-aged adults with untreated hearing loss scored worse on memory, attention and thinking tests than those with normal hearing.
ai.summary: Researchers compared 48 adults aged 40–65, half with normal hearing and half with untreated hearing loss. Those with hearing loss performed significantly worse on all cognitive tasks, with larger gaps in memory, category fluency and attention accuracy.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests hearing health in midlife may be linked to everyday thinking abilities, so noticing and addressing hearing problems early could matter for long-term brain health.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you are struggling to hear in everyday situations and consider getting a hearing check from a qualified professional.
ai.fact: Better-ear pure-tone thresholds independently predicted cognitive performance in this study, while age and education did not.

quiz.question: What did the study find about adults with untreated hearing loss compared with those with normal hearing?
quiz.answer: They performed significantly poorer on all the cognitive tasks assessed.

ai.caveat: This was a small, cross-sectional study, so it cannot show whether hearing loss causes cognitive decline or whether the relationship works the other way.

items.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

ai.headline: A new training method helps robots learn long, multi-step tasks more efficiently by breaking them into smaller parts.
ai.summary: The study tested AtomicRL, a reinforcement-learning framework that breaks complex robotic tasks into atomic subtasks and focuses practice on the weakest steps. It improved performance on simulated long-horizon benchmarks and real-world robot tasks compared with a standard method.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how breaking big goals into smaller, mastered steps can improve learning, which applies to people tackling complex skills too.
ai.life_skill: Break a complex skill you want to learn into small steps and practise the weakest one first.
ai.fact: Breaking long-horizon robotic tasks into atomic subtasks and targeting bottlenecks improved performance over standard reinforcement learning in the tested benchmarks.

quiz.question: What did AtomicRL do to improve robot learning on long tasks?
quiz.answer: It broke tasks into atomic subtasks, prevented credit from failed subtasks spreading across boundaries, and focused practice on the weakest steps.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the results come from simulated benchmarks and limited real-world robot tests, so they are not proof that the method works broadly.

items.title: Cache Engineering for Agents

ai.headline: New cache-control methods let AI agents manage memory without rewriting history, cutting cost and speeding up responses.
ai.summary: The paper studies how large language model agents handle long sequences of observations and actions. It finds that letting agents drop selected cache entries and reposition retained ones improves benchmark scores by 1.7 points and reduces average cost by 27.7% compared with conventional summarisation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI tools people use every day could become cheaper and faster while handling longer tasks.
ai.life_skill: Notice when an AI assistant forgets earlier parts of a long conversation and start a new thread with a brief summary if needed.
ai.fact: LLM agents can exceed their maximum context length as task trajectories grow.

quiz.question: What did the proposed cache engineering approach allow agents to do without modifying the trajectory?
quiz.answer: It allowed agents to proactively drop selected cache entries and adjust retained keys' position encodings.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Infantile amnesia results from differential memory retrieval in humans

ai.headline: Early childhood memories may still exist but become harder to retrieve over time.
ai.summary: Researchers tested toddlers aged 18–24 months on memory tasks over up to six months. They found that forgetting was mixed: some toddlers kept full memories, some lost them completely, and about a quarter kept only part. A brain signal linked to retrieval predicted who kept full memories, and maternal immune activation during pregnancy appeared to affect how vulnerable children were to forgetting.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that forgetting in early childhood may be about losing access to memories rather than the memories never forming.
ai.life_skill: Notice that not remembering something from early childhood does not necessarily mean the experience never happened.
ai.fact: Infantile amnesia is the most common form of forgetting in mammals.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find about toddlers’ memories over time?
quiz.answer: Some toddlers kept full memories, some lost them completely, and nearly a quarter kept only part of the memory.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Family Educational and Cultural Practices Amplify Rather than Buffer Socioeconomic Inequalities in Academic Achievement in France

ai.headline: Family educational practices may widen, not narrow, school achievement gaps linked to family background in France.
ai.summary: Researchers followed 12,904 French students from Grade 5 to Grade 9 and looked at family background and home learning practices such as cultural outings, extracurricular activities, parental involvement in school, and shared parent–child activities. Family background strongly predicted achievement, and while home practices had some positive links, they tended to benefit students from higher-background families more, suggesting they may reinforce rather than reduce inequalities.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that resources available at home can shape school outcomes in ways that may deepen existing gaps between students from different family backgrounds.
ai.life_skill: Notice what learning resources and activities are available at home and consider how they might support schoolwork.
ai.fact: In this French study, family educational practices were generally more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds than for those from lower backgrounds.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that family practices cause the differences in achievement.

items.title: Scales for Evaluating Self-Regulated Learning and Social-Behavioral Skills in Children with Learning Disabilities

ai.headline: Researchers created and tested two scales to measure self-regulation and social skills in children with learning disabilities.
ai.summary: The study used data from 469 primary school students in Turkey to develop two assessment scales: one for self-regulated learning and one for social skills and adaptive behaviour. Both scales were found to be valid and reliable through statistical testing, with internal consistency coefficients ranging from 0.71 to 0.83.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how educators can identify and support students who struggle with managing their own learning and social behaviour.
ai.life_skill: Notice how you plan and stay motivated when doing schoolwork, and consider which strategies help you adjust in social situations.
ai.fact: Two new scales were developed to assess self-regulated learning and social-behavioral skills in students with specific learning disabilities.

quiz.question: How many primary school students provided data for this study?
quiz.answer: Data from 469 primary school students in Turkey were used.

ai.caveat: The study was conducted in Turkey with a specific group of students, so the scales may not work the same way for all children everywhere.

items.title: Teen depression and anxiety predicted by childhood brain development

ai.headline: Brain development predicts teen depression
ai.summary: Researchers analyzed 30,000 brain scans to study childhood brain development and its effects on mental health. They found a detailed timeline of brain maturation and potential consequences of disruption. The study hints at a link between childhood brain development and teen depression and anxiety.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding brain development can help identify risk factors for mental health issues in teenagers
ai.life_skill: Notice changes in your mood and talk to a trusted adult if you're struggling
ai.fact: Childhood brain development is linked to mental health in teenagers

quiz.question: What was analyzed to study childhood brain development?
quiz.answer: Nearly 30,000 brain scans were analyzed

ai.caveat: The study's findings are based on observational data and do not prove causation

items.title: War and military mobilisation are drivers of climate change

ai.headline: War drives climate change
ai.summary: The relationship between war and climate change was examined, revealing that war and military mobilisation contribute to climate change. The concept of climate change as a 'threat multiplier' was discussed, highlighting its potential to provoke armed conflict. However, it was argued that this framing ignores the role of war as a climate change multiplier.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the link between war and climate change is crucial for addressing the growing threat of climate change to global security and stability.
ai.life_skill: Consider the environmental impact of military actions
ai.fact: War and military mobilisation are drivers of climate change

quiz.question: What is the relationship between war and climate change?
quiz.answer: War and military mobilisation are drivers of climate change.

ai.caveat: This study is based on commentary and theory, and more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between war and climate change.

items.title: Data vital in holding militaries accountable for the environmental toll of war

ai.headline: Accurate data on military greenhouse gas emissions is needed to hold armed forces accountable for war's environmental impact.
ai.summary: An expert writing in The BMJ's climate issue argues that accurate data on greenhouse gas emissions during armed conflict is urgently needed. The goal is to hold militaries, governments and individuals accountable for the environmental impact of war ahead of COP31 in Turkiye.

ai.fact: A jury ruled in favor of David Sabatini in a $6 million defamation lawsuit.

quiz.question: Who won the defamation lawsuit described in the report?
quiz.answer: Biologist David Sabatini won the lawsuit.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a single legal verdict, not scientific research, so it does not establish general facts about harassment claims.

items.title: In Vivo Aquaporin-1 Circular RNA Therapy for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia
authors: Henry T. HoffmanUniversity of Iowa, Iowa CityHarry QuonJohns Hopkins University, BaltimoreChristopher H. RassekhUniversity of Pennsylvania, PhiladelphiaHariz HassanRiboX Therapeutics, Cambridge, MA

ai.headline: Circular RNA therapy helps xerostomia
ai.summary: Researchers studied aquaporin-1 circular RNA therapy for radiation-induced xerostomia, finding potential benefits. The study explored a new treatment approach. Results show promise for alleviating symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it could improve treatment for people with radiation-induced dry mouth
ai.life_skill: Try asking your doctor about new therapies for xerostomia
ai.fact: Aquaporin-1 is linked to water transport in cells

quiz.question: What condition did the circular RNA therapy target?
quiz.answer: Radiation-induced xerostomia

ai.caveat: The study's findings are not yet proven in humans and require further research

items.title: Physical activity guidelines’ impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials

ai.headline: Exercise meeting MS physical activity guidelines may improve processing speed and memory.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials with 462 people with multiple sclerosis looked at whether meeting physical activity guidelines affects cognition. It found significant improvements in processing speed, visuospatial memory, and verbal memory compared with controls.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that regular physical activity at guideline levels could help people with MS maintain thinking skills that matter for daily life.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular physical activity into your week if you have MS, after checking with a qualified health professional what is safe for you.
ai.fact: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic disease associated with inflammation and cognitive decline.

quiz.question: Which thinking skills improved significantly when people with MS met physical activity guidelines?
quiz.answer: Processing speed, visuospatial memory, and verbal memory improved significantly.

ai.caveat: The findings came from a limited number of studies with a high risk of bias, so more trials are needed.

items.title: AI-powered risk prediction models for preventable maternal mortality in rural settings: a systematic review.
items.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making

ai.headline: AI predicts maternal mortality
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed AI models that predict maternal mortality in rural areas. They found that these models can accurately predict mortality when trained on large datasets. However, the models have methodological weaknesses and limited real-world applicability.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because reducing maternal mortality is a major global health goal, and AI models could help achieve this goal in rural areas with limited access to healthcare.
ai.life_skill: Try to learn about global health initiatives and how technology can improve healthcare outcomes.
ai.fact: Maternal mortality remains disproportionately high in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in rural settings.

quiz.question: What is the main goal of using AI models in this context?
quiz.answer: To predict and reduce preventable maternal mortality in rural areas.

ai.caveat: The models have methodological weaknesses, such as inadequate external validation and calibration assessment, which limit confidence in their generalizability.

items.title: Parental attitudes and adolescent empathy in a rural sociocultural context in Türkiye

ai.headline: In rural Türkiye, adolescents who perceived more authoritarian parenting reported lower empathy.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 458 high school students aged 14–18 in Bingöl about perceived parenting attitudes and empathy. Authoritarian parenting was linked to lower empathy, while protective/demanding parenting showed a small positive link; democratic parenting showed no link.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that parenting styles linked to empathy in Western research may not work the same way in traditional family settings elsewhere.
ai.life_skill: Notice how controlling or supportive your parents’ attitudes feel, and consider discussing expectations calmly with them.
ai.fact: Authoritarian parenting was negatively associated with adolescent empathy in this rural Turkish sample.

quiz.question: Which parenting attitude was linked to lower empathy in the study?
quiz.answer: Authoritarian parenting was negatively associated with empathy.

ai.caveat: This was a single cross-sectional study, so it cannot show that parenting causes changes in empathy.

items.title: Dysfunctional Sleep Beliefs and Attitudes in Major Depressive Disorder: Dimensional Associations with Clinical Phenotypes and Gut-Neuroimmune-Metabolic-Oxidative Pathways

ai.headline: In people with major depression, certain sleep beliefs are linked to illness severity, suicidality, and body chemistry.
ai.summary: Researchers compared sleep beliefs in 87 people hospitalised with major depressive disorder and 31 healthy controls. People with depression scored lower on some sleep-belief dimensions, and a combined score was linked to lower insomnia severity, lower depression severity, fewer physical symptoms, less suicidal thinking, and fewer illness recurrences, as well as to markers of inflammation, oxidative stress and gut chemicals.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how people think about sleep may be connected to wider mental and physical health processes in depression.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your beliefs about sleep affect your mood and discuss any unhelpful sleep thoughts with a qualified mental health professional.
ai.fact: Dysfunctional sleep beliefs in major depressive disorder are associated with illness severity, suicidality, recurrence, and neuroimmune-metabolic-oxidative alterations.

quiz.question: What was the combined sleep-belief score linked to in people with major depression?
quiz.answer: It was inversely associated with insomnia severity, overall depression severity, physical symptoms, current suicidal ideation and illness recurrence.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the study only shows associations, not cause and effect.

items.title: Tutorbot pilot study: learning support, feedback and assessment in a crisis intervention module

ai.headline: Tutorbots aid psychology students
ai.summary: Researchers studied how postgraduate students used a tutorbot in a crisis intervention module. The tutorbot was mainly used for learning and concept clarification. It provided formative scaffolding and multilingual support, but sometimes frustrated students with its Socratic style.
ai.why_it_matters: This study matters because it shows how AI can support teaching in higher education, particularly in multilingual settings.
ai.life_skill: Try using AI tools as a supplement to, not replacement for, human teaching and guidance.
ai.fact: Tutorbots can function as formative tools in a supervised academic environment.

quiz.question: What was the main use of the tutorbot by students?
quiz.answer: The tutorbot was mainly used for module content-related learning and concept clarification.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint pilot study, not yet peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: “I will not accept to bury my pig”: Taenia solium, WASH, and gender roles in the smallholder pork value chain in Southern Province, Rwanda

ai.headline: In rural Rwanda, gender roles and poor water and sanitation create gaps that let a pig tapeworm spread between people and pigs.
ai.summary: Researchers held focus groups with 44 men and women across Rwanda’s pork value chain and interviewed six key informants. They found women mainly cared for pigs while men handled pens, buying, selling, slaughtering and butchering, and that free-range pigs, human waste reuse, informal slaughter and undercooked pork were common biosecurity gaps.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday roles and living conditions can affect the spread of diseases shared between animals and people.
ai.life_skill: Check that pork is thoroughly cooked before eating it.
ai.fact: Taenia solium is a tapeworm that can infect both people and pigs and can cause serious illness and income losses.

quiz.question: What did participants say was a major barrier to controlling the tapeworm in Rwanda’s pork value chain?
quiz.answer: Poverty was identified as a major barrier.

ai.caveat: This is a small qualitative study from one district, so its findings cannot be generalised or taken as proof of cause and effect.

items.title: Conflicted Records: Typed Adversarial Contracts for Auditable LLM Output Quality Enforcement

ai.headline: A multi-model adversarial checking system can catch LLM errors that standard checks miss, with an auditable record trail.
ai.summary: The paper studies LLM-generated records that can be both correct and wrong at the same time, such as a true fact next to a hallucination. BiasGuard-D uses two adversarial AI roles from different model families, a three-model quorum vote, and combined referential-plus-semantic checks to detect defects; on HaluEval QA it raised right-answer recovery by 49 percentage points.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI outputs might be checked more reliably and transparently as they become part of everyday information systems.
ai.life_skill: Check important AI-generated information against a second source before relying on it.
ai.fact: A single LLM-generated record can simultaneously contain a grounded fact and a hallucination.

quiz.question: What did BiasGuard-D add to catch errors that referential checks miss?
quiz.answer: It added a semantic component that fires on verdicts referential checks miss.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the results come from a proposed system evaluated on a specific QA benchmark rather than independent real-world trials.

items.title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures

ai.headline: AI enhances low-resolution videos
ai.summary: Researchers studied creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse captures. They proposed a framework called RealMe, which enhances limited captures into high-resolution videos. RealMe outperforms state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity and consistency.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it could improve video production and consumption in everyday life and various industries.
ai.life_skill: Try exploring AI video editing tools to enhance your own videos.
ai.fact: RealMe is a unified framework that enhances low-resolution videos into high-resolution, 4D-consistent videos.

quiz.question: What is the name of the proposed framework?
quiz.answer: The proposed framework is called RealMe.

ai.caveat: The study is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Developmental trajectories organize the assembly of valence circuits in the central amygdala

ai.headline: Developmental trajectories shape amygdala circuits
ai.summary: Researchers studied how neural circuits in the central amygdala develop. They found that developmental trajectories organize the assembly of valence-specific circuits. These trajectories give rise to future appetitive and aversive neurons.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how neural circuits develop can help explain how emotions and behaviors are formed
ai.life_skill: Notice how your emotions and behaviors develop over time
ai.fact: The central amygdala contains distinct neural circuits for appetitive and aversive behaviors

quiz.question: What part of the brain do the researchers study?
quiz.answer: The central amygdala

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution

items.title: The CTF is dead, long live the CTF? Exploring perspectives on AI and the recognition of skill in capture-the-flag competitions

ai.headline: AI is changing how capture-the-flag competitions signal skill and how security learners are judged.
ai.summary: This exploratory qualitative study interviewed seven experienced CTF organisers and players and received eleven anonymous written responses. Participants disagreed about AI’s role, with some criticising AI-assisted solving, others wanting AI built into competitions, and many noting that rankings now reflect access to AI and money, while some students solved challenges without being able to explain how.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how automation can weaken the value of a skill measure and force communities to rethink what counts as genuine ability.
ai.life_skill: Try explaining how you solved a problem, not just getting the right answer.
ai.fact: Capture-the-flag competitions are used to recruit talent, build skills and sustain a competitive culture in the security community.

quiz.question: What did some participants say about students who solved CTF challenges quickly with AI?
quiz.answer: They could solve challenges quickly but could not explain how they had done so.

ai.caveat: This is a small, exploratory preprint based on interviews and written responses, not yet peer reviewed, so its findings are not proof.

items.title: Comparing the Impact of Augmented Reality and Electronic Popular Science Picture Books on Vocabulary and Reading in Preschool Children

ai.headline: Electronic picture books helped preschoolers learn science words better, while augmented reality books boosted motivation and deeper understanding.
ai.summary: Sixty-two children aged 5-6 were randomly assigned to read popular science picture books either as augmented reality books or electronic books over two weeks. The electronic group scored higher on target vocabulary, explicit reading comprehension and physical engagement, while the augmented reality group showed stronger implicit reading comprehension, intrinsic motivation, verbal engagement and emotional engagement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that different digital reading formats can support different kinds of learning, so choosing the right format may depend on whether the goal is learning facts or building motivation and deeper understanding.
ai.life_skill: Try matching the reading format to your goal: use simple electronic books for learning new words and facts, and more interactive formats to spark curiosity and deeper thinking.
ai.fact: Physical and verbal engagement helped explain how multimedia reading media influenced reading comprehension in this study.
ai.caveat: The study involved only 62 children aged 5-6 over two weeks, so the results may not apply to older children, longer periods, or other subjects.

items.title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea

ai.headline: Enzyme-embedded compostable plastics break down almost completely in the deep sea while keeping their strength.
ai.summary: The study tested compostable polyesters with enzymes embedded using heat. These materials degraded nearly completely in deep-sea conditions and across marine environments without losing their performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible way to reduce long-lasting plastic pollution in oceans while still using durable materials.
ai.life_skill: Check whether plastic items are labelled compostable before choosing them.
ai.fact: Thermal enzyme embedding can greatly speed up the breakdown of compostable polyesters in marine environments.

quiz.question: What happened to the enzyme-embedded compostable polyesters in the deep sea?
quiz.answer: They showed near-complete degradation while preserving material performance.

ai.caveat: This is a single materials study, so real-world results may vary and it does not prove all enzyme-embedded plastics will behave the same way.

items.title: Conflict and climate change are driving food shortages

ai.headline: Conflict and climate change drive food shortages
ai.summary: Researchers studied global food security and found that conflict and climate change are driving localised food shortages. Despite increased global calorie production, conflict affects food production, access, and affordability. The Food and Agriculture Organization identified 13 countries with expected increases in acute food insecurity.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because food shortages have long-term negative impacts on health, particularly in areas affected by conflict and climate change.
ai.life_skill: Check how your daily food choices might impact global food security.
ai.fact: Conflict and climate change are linked to food shortages worldwide.

quiz.question: What are the main drivers of localised food shortages?
quiz.answer: Conflict and climate change are the main drivers of localised food shortages.

ai.caveat: This study is based on a report and may not be a comprehensive or peer-reviewed analysis of the issue.

items.title: Study finds air quality warnings had only a modest impact on Montrealers' movements during wildfires

ai.headline: Air quality warnings during wildfires changed Montrealers' travel only modestly.
ai.summary: The study looked at Montrealers' travel patterns during Canada's worst wildfire smoke episodes when Environment and Climate Change Canada urged people to limit outdoor activity. Movement did change, but far less than public health officials might have hoped.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that warnings alone may not be enough to change how people behave during smoky wildfire conditions.
ai.life_skill: Check local air quality alerts and consider reducing outdoor activity when smoke levels are high.
ai.fact: Public health warnings during wildfire smoke episodes led to only modest changes in travel patterns in Montreal.

quiz.question: How much did air quality warnings affect Montrealers' movements during wildfires?
quiz.answer: They had only a modest impact on travel patterns.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on observed travel patterns during specific wildfire episodes and cannot prove the warnings caused the changes.

items.title: Novel but stable endosymbionts have contrasting effects on aphid dispersal and plant feeding damage in the cereal pest Diuraphis noxia

ai.headline: Certain bacteria inside aphids can change how much crop damage they cause and whether they spread.
ai.summary: Researchers put two types of bacteria into Russian wheat aphids, a cereal pest. One bacterium made feeding damage and aphid numbers worse, while the other reduced both; the first also stopped aphids from growing wings and dispersing.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how tiny organisms living inside insects can influence crop damage and pest spread, which matters for food production.
ai.fact: Endosymbiotic bacteria can alter aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley and affect whether aphids develop wings and disperse.

quiz.question: What did the two bacteria do differently to aphid feeding damage?
quiz.answer: Rickettsiella increased feeding damage while Regiella reduced it.

ai.caveat: This is a single controlled experiment in one aphid species, so the results may not apply to other pests or field conditions.

items.title: Use green transition funds to achieve health for all, suggest experts

ai.headline: Experts say green energy transition funds could help pay for universal health coverage in poorer countries.
ai.summary: The article reports expert opinion in The BMJ's climate issue that money from the green energy transition could be used to finance universal health coverage in low- and middle-income countries.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how climate spending might also improve health and reduce inequality around the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how money spent on one problem, such as climate change, can sometimes help solve another, such as access to healthcare.
ai.fact: Universal health coverage means everyone can get the health services they need without financial hardship.

quiz.question: What do experts suggest green transition funds could help achieve in low- and middle-income countries?
quiz.answer: They suggest the funds could help finance universal health coverage.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about expert opinion, not a research study with data or proof.

items.title: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave

ai.headline: Scientists found a rare, eyeless cave snail in China, with only three living adults seen.
ai.summary: Researchers explored a high-altitude cave in China and discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail adapted to live entirely in darkness. It is the first recorded discovery of its kind in China, and only three living adults were found.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how little we still know about hidden underground life and how quickly rare species can be at risk.

quiz.question: How many living adults of the new snail species did researchers find?
quiz.answer: Researchers found only three living adults.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a single discovery, not a peer-reviewed study, so details are limited.

items.title: Electronic Quitline Referral With Enhanced Academic Detailing for the Promotion of Smoking Cessation

ai.headline: Quitline eReferral aids smoking cessation
ai.summary: This phase IV clinical trial studied the impact of an electronic Quitline referral system on smoking cessation. The system was implemented with an enhanced academic detailing strategy in community health centers. The trial examined the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of this approach.
ai.why_it_matters: This research matters because it could help increase tobacco cessation treatment among disadvantaged patients who use tobacco.
ai.life_skill: Try seeking help from a Quitline if you want to stop smoking.
ai.fact: Smoking is linked to tobacco-related carcinoma.

quiz.question: What was the main goal of this clinical trial?
quiz.answer: To determine the impact of an electronic Quitline referral system on Quitline reach and self-reported quit rates.

ai.caveat: The results may not be generalizable to all populations or settings until further studies are conducted.

items.title: Future in mind: Systematic review of compassion-based interventions in higher education and feasibility study of Compassionate Mind Training with pre-registration Mental Health Student Nurses
items.venue: Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)

ai.headline: Compassion-based training may be acceptable and feasible for student nurses, but more trials are needed.
ai.summary: A review of 33 studies involving 4,897 higher education students looked at how compassion-based interventions are recruited and delivered. A separate small feasibility study of Compassionate Mind Training with 38 first-year mental health student nurses found high acceptability and positive wellbeing measure responses, though it was not a randomised trial.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how student wellbeing support might be tested and improved in demanding courses like nursing.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing when you are self-critical and respond to yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend.
ai.fact: Compassion-based interventions are being studied as ways to prevent and address psychological problems in higher education students.

quiz.question: What did the feasibility study find about Compassionate Mind Training for student nurses?
quiz.answer: Participants rated it highly on enjoyableness, usefulness and clarity, and qualitative feedback indicated it was acceptable.

ai.caveat: The student nurse study was small, single-group and quasi-experimental, so it cannot prove the training caused the improvements.

items.title: Effects of dance-based physical activity on cognitive and psychological health across age groups: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Dance-based activity may help some thinking and mood outcomes, especially in older adults, but evidence is mixed.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 22 controlled trials with 1,645 people aged 4 to 94 looked at dance-based physical activity. It found some favourable links with global cognition, memory, attention, depression, anxiety, stress, well-being and quality of life, but results were inconsistent and executive function findings were mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows dance could be a low-cost way to support mental and cognitive health, though stronger evidence is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Try joining a regular dance or movement class to see if it helps your mood and focus.
ai.fact: Dance-based physical activity combines motor, cognitive, emotional and social elements.

quiz.question: What did the review find about executive function?
quiz.answer: Findings for executive function were mixed.

ai.caveat: Many studies had a high risk of bias, samples were small, and most evidence came from older adults, so firm conclusions cannot be drawn.

items.title: Effects of Active Video Games on Cardiometabolic Health in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

ai.headline: Active video games may slightly lower BMI and blood pressure in children and teens.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 14 randomised trials with 942 children and adolescents aged 4-18. Active video games were linked to small reductions in body mass index and systolic blood pressure, while effects on other heart and metabolism measures were uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that active video games can be a fun way to add movement and may support heart health in young people.
ai.life_skill: Try swapping some seated screen time for active video games that get you moving.
ai.fact: Active video games were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure in children and adolescents.

quiz.question: What did active video games reduce in children and adolescents according to the review?
quiz.answer: They were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure.

ai.caveat: The evidence is based on a limited number of trials and certainty for many outcomes remains uncertain.

items.title: The Role of Community Pharmacists in Identifying and Managing Insomnia and Facilitating Access to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) – a Systematic Review

ai.headline: Community pharmacists may help identify insomnia and guide people toward CBT-I, but this is not yet common practice.
ai.summary: A systematic review of nine studies looked at how community pharmacists manage chronic insomnia. It found pharmacists could spot insomnia during counselling, reduce inappropriate sleeping medicines, and signpost or deliver CBT-I, though standard protocols, referral routes and time are lacking.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible way to get evidence-based sleep help more easily through a local pharmacy rather than only a GP or specialist.
ai.life_skill: If you struggle with sleep, ask your community pharmacist whether they can screen for insomnia or point you to CBT-I.
ai.fact: Insomnia affects approximately 10% of the global adult population.

quiz.question: What did the review find about community pharmacists and insomnia?
quiz.answer: They could identify insomnia, deprescribe inappropriate hypnotics, and in some settings deliver or signpost patients to CBT-I.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the included studies were limited by a lack of standardised protocols, referral pathways and time constraints.

items.title: Family Educational and Cultural Practices Amplify Rather than Buffer Socioeconomic Inequalities in Academic Achievement in France

ai.headline: Family educational practices may widen, not narrow, school achievement gaps linked to family background in France.
ai.summary: Researchers followed 12,904 French students from Grade 5 to Grade 9 and looked at family background and home educational practices such as cultural activities and parental involvement. Practices were linked to higher achievement overall, but when they made a difference they tended to help students from higher-background families more, reinforcing rather than reducing gaps.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that extra home support does not automatically close achievement gaps and can sometimes make them wider.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the extra educational activities you do at home are helping everyone equally or mainly those who already have advantages.
ai.fact: In this French study, family educational practices were generally more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds.

quiz.question: Did family educational practices mainly reduce or reinforce socioeconomic achievement gaps in this study?
quiz.answer: They tended to reinforce gaps by being more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that family practices cause the achievement patterns.

items.title: Engagement or disengagement: understanding the emotional dynamics of EFL learners in GenAI-assisted writing from the sociocultural perspective

ai.headline: Students' feelings about using AI for English writing change over time and differ from person to person.
ai.summary: Researchers followed three Chinese university students learning English as a foreign language over a 14-week course that used generative AI for writing tasks. They found three different emotional patterns: one student stayed mostly positive, one moved from practical disengagement to critical engagement, and one moved from moderate disengagement to a breakdown and stronger disengagement. These patterns were shaped by a mix of personal factors, such as English proficiency and AI literacy, and environmental factors, such as task design and teacher or peer support.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools do not affect every learner's emotions in the same way, so support needs to be tailored to individual students.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your own feelings change when you use AI for schoolwork and ask a teacher or peer for help if you become discouraged.
ai.fact: Emotional engagement with AI-assisted writing is a dynamic and fluid state that interacts with behavioural and cognitive engagement over time.

quiz.question: What did the study find about students' emotional engagement with GenAI-assisted writing?
quiz.answer: It found three distinct trajectories—positive-resilient, pragmatic-transformative, and vulnerable-contingent—shaped by individual and environmental factors.

ai.caveat: The findings come from only three students in one course, so they may not apply to all learners or settings.

items.title: PI-MLLM: Psychophysics-Inspired Multimodal Large Language Model for Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis

ai.headline: A new AI model uses physical sensory cues to better predict emotions from oddly satisfying videos.
ai.summary: Researchers built a dataset of 12,000 short oddly satisfying videos labelled for viewer emotion under video-only, audio-only and audio-visual conditions. They then created PI-MLLM, an AI model that aligns visual motion and sound cues and uses Shapley attribution to show which sense drives the emotion. Tests suggest it improves emotion prediction and sensory-grounded explanations.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how sight and sound together shape feelings from everyday online videos, helping us understand digital media effects.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether a video’s feeling comes from what you see, what you hear, or both together.
ai.fact: Oddly satisfying videos can evoke strong responses through repetitive motion, visual tactility and ASMR-like sounds despite few explicit emotion cues.

quiz.question: What does PI-MLLM use Shapley attribution for?
quiz.answer: To identify the dominant modality and determine whether visual and auditory evidence is synergistic or conflicting.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the findings come from experiments on a newly constructed dataset rather than independent confirmation.

items.title: Examining the roles of socioeconomic status and relevant health correlates (body mass index, diet quality, and inflammation) for neuropsychological function in young adults

ai.headline: Higher body mass index and more sugar or fat in the diet are linked to lower cognitive performance in young adults.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 109 young adults to see whether body mass index, inflammation, or diet explained the link between socioeconomic status and thinking skills. Body mass index did not explain that link, but higher body mass index and higher sugar and fat intake were linked to lower cognitive scores. Sugar intake appeared to partly link body mass index to cognition, but this disappeared after adjusting for other factors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that everyday eating habits and body weight may be connected to how well young adults think, even if the exact causes are still unclear.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different foods and meals affect your energy and concentration, and consider eating more balanced meals.
ai.fact: Higher body mass index and higher sugar and fat intake were inversely correlated with cognitive functioning in this sample of young adults.

quiz.question: Did body mass index explain the link between socioeconomic status and cognition?
quiz.answer: No, BMI did not account for the association between SES and cognition.

ai.caveat: This was a small cross-sectional study of 109 young adults, so it cannot show cause and effect.

items.title: A Mechanistic Theory Unifying Value and Schema in the Prefrontal Cortex

ai.headline: A new brain model suggests value signals control how we use learned context to make flexible choices.
ai.summary: The paper studies how the prefrontal cortex handles both value and world structure. It proposes that value acts as a control signal gating structured working memory of the current context to guide behaviour, rather than simply reading out actions. Recurrent neural networks trained with reinforcement or supervised learning reproduced this model across value-based tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a fresh way to understand how people adapt decisions in new situations using what they already know about the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice when a familiar pattern helps you make a quick choice in a new situation.
ai.fact: The prefrontal cortex is involved in both computing value and learning the structure of the world.

quiz.question: In the proposed model, what role does value play in behaviour?
quiz.answer: Value acts as a control signal that gates structured working memory of the current context to control behaviour.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and based on computational models rather than direct human evidence.

items.title: Transparency, accountability, and scholarly integrity: A systematic narrative review of artificial intelligence governance frameworks in healthcare publication

ai.headline: Guidance on using AI in healthcare publishing has grown but remains fragmented and uneven in authority.
ai.summary: The review examined 100 publications on how AI should be reported and governed in healthcare research, including 69 guidelines, frameworks and policies. It found guidance has shifted from focusing on AI model performance to wider issues such as fairness, transparency, human oversight and generative AI, but the landscape remains fragmented with varying levels of authority.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how scientific research involving AI is being steered, which affects the reliability of health information people may encounter.
ai.life_skill: Check whether health research you read discloses how AI was used and follow guidance from qualified professionals for health decisions.
ai.fact: Guidance on AI in healthcare publications has evolved from model performance transparency toward broader sociotechnical accountability between 2018 and 2026.

quiz.question: What did the review find about AI governance in healthcare publications?
quiz.answer: It found the guidance has evolved toward broader accountability but remains fragmented and uneven in authority.

ai.caveat: This is a single systematic narrative review, so its synthesis reflects the included sources and search window rather than definitive proof.

items.title: Submission Timing in Take-Home Exams, Procrastination Perceptions, and Their Impact on Grades

ai.headline: Submitting take-home exams neither too early nor too late may be linked to better grades.
